items.title: 6 Ghanaian victims of human trafficking arrested in Zambia cybercrime raid – Foreign Affairs Ministry
items.description: The Ministry of Foreign Affairs has cautioned Ghanaians seeking employment opportunities in Zambia following the arrest of six Ghanaian nationals during a joint operation targeting suspected organised cybercrime in Lusaka. The Ministry said the arrests highlight a worrying trend in which unsuspecting Ghanaians are allegedly lured to Zambia with promises of legitimate jobs before being subjected to coercive conditions and forced into cybercrime activities. The six Ghanaians were among 79 people arrested on August 23, 2026, during a joint operation by the Zambia Police Service, the Drug Enforcement Commission (DEC) and the Department of Immigration. The operation targeted a facility suspected of being involved in organised cybercrime. The 79 individuals arrested included 10 Zambians and 69 foreign nationals, among them the six Ghanaians. In a travel advisory issued on Monday, the Ministry said it had “observed with concern the emerging trend of Ghanaians being lured to Zambia through fraudulent employment opportunities and subsequently being subjected to coercive conditions and forced involvement in cybercrime activities.” According to the Ministry, information received by the Ghana High Commission in Lusaka indicates that some of the affected individuals were recruited through purportedly legitimate employment opportunities, including online data-entry jobs. However, upon arriving in Zambia, some were allegedly forced to participate in online scam activities after their passports were confiscated by their employers. The Ministry said the development demonstrates how human-trafficking syndicates are increasingly exploiting legitimate-looking job offers to lure unsuspecting job seekers into illegal activities. “The above situation highlights the growing use of fraudulent employment opportunities by human trafficking syndicates to lure unsuspecting job seekers into illicit activities,” the Ministry said. The Foreign Affairs Ministry has urged Ghanaians planning to travel to Zambia for employment to exercise extreme caution and conduct thorough checks before accepting job offers. It advised prospective workers to verify the authenticity of employment offers, recruitment agencies and prospective employers before making travel arrangements. The Ministry also urged Ghanaians already living in Zambia to remain vigilant, particularly when responding to employment opportunities advertised online. “Ghanaians living in Zambia are also urged to remain vigilant, exercise caution when responding to online employment opportunities, and maintain regular contact with the Ghana High Commission in Lusaka for consular assistance if the need arises,” the advisory stated. The Ministry further urged Ghanaians to seek assistance from the Ghana High Commission in Lusaka whenever they find themselves in difficulty. It reaffirmed the government’s commitment to protecting the welfare and interests of Ghanaians travelling to or residing outside the country. “The Ministry wishes to use this opportunity to reiterate government’s commitment to safeguarding the welfare and interests of Ghanaians travelling to or residing abroad,” it said.

items.title: ‘Why we couldn’t rescue Air Force aircraft crash victims’ – lgbokoda residents
items.description: By Dayo Johnson, AKURE Residents of Igbokoda in Ilaje Local Government Area of Ondo State have recounted how a Nigerian Air Force ATR-42 aircraft crashed in the community, killing all 32 persons on board. Read Also: Video: Ondo crash Air Force pilot dies 2 weeks after wedding The aircraft, with tail number NGR 931, had 25 passengers and 7 crew members on board. It was said to be on a routine mission from Benin to Lagos when it reportedly lost contact with Air Traffic Controllers at about 9:13 a.m. on Monday, October 5, 2026, before crashing in a swampy area close to the Naval Base in Igbokoda. Search and rescue operations were immediately activated by the Nigerian Air Force, while security operatives cordoned off the crash site. President Bola Tinubu has ordered a probe into the incident, while Naval authorities have disclosed the identities of the casualties. Ondo State Governor, Lucky Aiyedatiwa, has also directed the State Emergency Management Agency, SEMA; the Ministry of Health and relevant security agencies to mobilize and provide full logistical and human support to the Nigerian Air Force and other emergency responders at the crash site. The governor, who said he has been in contact with the leadership of the Nigerian Air Force, the Chairman of Ilaje Local Government, Hon. Maurice Oripelaye, and security agencies on ground, expressed heartfelt sympathy to the Chief of Air Staff, the entire Nigerian Air Force family and families of all personnel and passengers on board. “Our thoughts and prayers are with them at this difficult time,” the governor said. He also urged residents of Igbokoda and adjoining communities to remain calm, cooperate with emergency responders and refrain from spreading unverified information. How it happened – Eyewitnesses Narrating how the incident happened, residents said it was drizzling when the crash occurred at about 9:40 a.m. on Monday. One of them, who identified himself as Jomiloju, said: “I was just trying to have my bath when I heard a loud noise. It was very frightening. “I rushed out and met other people in my area who heard the loud sound and equally rushed out of their houses to ascertain what happened. “We rushed towards the direction the sound came from and met many of our people there looking towards the swampy area within the community. “We had to sail to the location in canoes to have a good glimpse of the crashed plane. But all we saw was the wreckage. The larger part of the plane was deep inside the swamp. “After we discovered that we couldn’t help rescue any of the occupants, we sailed back to the river bank. The naval officers and police also sailed to the location in their speed boats.” Another resident, Lucky, said: “We have tried our best to rescue them, but the aircraft was deeply buried inside the swamp. Our people here have tried a lot. Even the women and men took their canoes and crossed to that place to rescue them. “We tried our best, but unfortunately we could not help the occupants. They were buried inside the swamp.” Similarly, Bolajoko Ayeni said: “Immediately it happened, there was nothing we could do. We just ran to the place. When we got there, we saw some parts like human parts. Then we just did some videos. “We couldn’t rescue anybody because the plane had already entered the swampy area. So there was nothing we could do. We just did the video and returned to land.” Vanguard News The post ‘Why we couldn’t rescue Air Force aircraft crash victims’ – lgbokoda residents appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Big Dawood leads clean-up, tree-planting campaign to tackle Accra’s sanitation challenges
items.description: Founder of Let Love Lead NGO, Dawood Akwesi Agyemang, popularly known as Big Dawood, is leading a community mobilisation effort to bring Ghanaians together for a clean-up and tree-planting exercise in Accra. The Green & Clean Initiative is scheduled for Wednesday, October 7, 2026, and will begin at Afrikiko Restaurant before continuing through Independence Avenue and ending at the State House Forecourt. Participants are expected to desilt choked drains, clean public spaces and plant more than 50 trees as part of a planned Green Legacy Corridor. The initiative forms part of Let Love Lead NGO’s broader Culture of Cleanliness Campaign, which the organisation says will run from 2027 to 2032. Speaking ahead of the exercise, Big Dawood said the campaign was intended to move discussions about Accra’s sanitation and flooding challenges towards practical community action. “Accra is flooded every year. Our drains are choked and our communities continue to face the consequences of poor environmental practices. This is not the responsibility of government alone. We are not complaining; we are cleaning and greening,” he said. He said the initiative would demonstrate what could be achieved when residents take collective responsibility for their surroundings. “We want to demonstrate that when citizens come together and take responsibility for their environment, we can make our communities safer and more resilient,” he added. Big Dawood has also called on organisations and community leaders to replicate similar initiatives in their communities, arguing that addressing flooding and the effects of climate change requires sustained collective action. The initiative has attracted support from public institutions, private-sector organisations and community groups. The Director of Diaspora Affairs at the Presidency, Kofi Okyere Darko, has endorsed the initiative and is expected to participate in the tree-planting exercise as part of the President’s Green Ghana agenda. Deputy Minister for Tourism, Culture and Creative Arts and Member of Parliament for Ayawaso North, Yussif Jajah, has also been invited as Special Guest and Host MP. He is expected to mobilise constituents, plant a Legacy Tree and speak on the importance of cleanliness to tourism and the Black Star Experience. Ghanaian music duo Keche, BuzStopBoys and A1 Diesel are also supporting the initiative. Beyond the October 7 exercise, organisers say the campaign will seek to encourage sustained youth participation in environmental activities, including priority consideration for 5,000 paid green jobs planned for 2027. Let Love Lead says the initiative forms part of its broader community-focused work on environmental sanitation, community mobilisation and civic responsibility. Big Dawood is urging Ghanaians to move beyond discussions about Accra’s environmental challenges and participate in efforts to clean, green and reclaim public spaces.

items.title: Dickson hails INEC, judiciary as NDC logo is uploaded
items.description: By Henry Umoru ABUJA- THE National Leader of the Nigeria Democratic Congress, NDC, Senator Seriake Dickson has congratulated the party’s leadership and Nigerians after the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) uploaded the party’s preferred and approved logo. In a statement posted on Facebook yesterday, the former Bayelsa State governor said the logo was uploaded by INEC in compliance with a High Court order, as provided for in the party’s constitution and ratified by its National Executive Committee (NEC). The Senator representing Bayelsa West hailed the Judiciary, INEC Chairman, Professor Joash Amupitan, and members of the INEC team for complying with the court judgment. He also thanked the NDC’s National Chairman, Senator Moses Cleopas, and NEC members for their hard work, just as he commended the understanding of the party’s candidates and members, adding that with the approved logo now uploaded, candidates could print campaign materials and continue their consultations and campaigns “with certainty”. He assured Nigerians and NDC candidates that the party was committed to seeing the matter through to the end. Dickson’s post read, “Congratulations to the entire leadership of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) and to all Nigerians, as the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) has uploaded our preferred and approved party logo, in compliance with the order of the High Court, as provided for in our Constitution and ratified by the National Executive Committee (NEC). “I thank the Nigerian Judiciary and the INEC Chairman, Professor Joash Amupitan, and all members of the INEC team for complying with the court judgment. “I thank the National Chairman of our great party, Senator Moses Cleopas, and the members of the NEC for their hard work. I also commend the understanding of all our candidates and members of the party. “Our approved logo has now been uploaded, and candidates can print campaign materials and continue their consultations and campaigns with certainty. “We assure all Nigerians and our candidates that we are committed to seeing this through to the end. We are fighters, and we will fight until the end. We have resisted those who sought to use the judiciary against the party, and they have failed. “We must now join hands and ensure that all candidates campaign and take their message freely to every part of Nigeria without intimidation. I call on all candidates to work with the party at all levels in the composition of their campaign teams as they are not independent candidates and AVOID SELF-SABOTAGE “We must together join hands to fight against propaganda and misinformation from people who seek to undermine the party and our candidates and create division with childish rumours. “The NDC is a product of vision, selfless dedication, and commitment to democratic ideals. We are prepared to fight to uphold the democratic rights of Nigerians and to ensure that multi-party democracy thrives. NDC all the way.” The post Dickson hails INEC, judiciary as NDC logo is uploaded appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Ondo ​‌‍‍‍‍⁠⁠‍​​‍‍⁠⁠​‍‌​deploys medical team, ambulances to NAF aircraft crash site
items.description: The Ondo State Government has deployed medical personnel and ambulances to the site of a Nigerian Air Force (NAF) aircraft crash in Igbokoda, Ilaje Local Government. The News Agency of Nigeria (NAN) report that the aircraft marked NAF-931 with 25 people on board on Monday plunged into a swampy area near the Naval Base in Igbokoda. The state Commissioner for Health, Dr Banji Ajaka, in a statement on Tuesday in Akure, said the ambulances were deployed from hospitals in Ilaje and Okitipupa Local Government areas on the directive of Gov. Lucky Aiyedatiwa. Ajaka said medical teams had been placed on alert while military personnel and other emergency responders continued recovery operations at the crash site. He said specialised equipment, including swamp buggies, had also been deployed to support the operation, urging the public to avoid spreading unverified information about the incident. “This is a national disaster that we shouldn’t play politics with,” Ajaka said, urging the public to wait for verified information. items.title: PM Shehbaz urges PTI to call off long march, resolve issues through dialogue
items.description: Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif on Tuesday urged the PTI to end its long march to Islamabad and invited the opposition to sit with the government to resolve contentious issues through political dialogue. The opposition has gone ahead with its march despite warnings from the Centre, which has vowed to prevent any gatherings in Islamabad. The protest aims to demand the release of jailed party founder and former prime minister Imran Khan. Addressing the groundbreaking ceremony of the Kashmir Chowk underpass in Islamabad on Tuesday, the premier said it was “unfortunate” that the “dreadful shadows” of long marches were hovering again, despite the PML-N and the PPP making efforts to engage the PTI in talks. The two parties, the prime minister said, held talks for two days in National Assembly Speaker Ayaz Sadiq’s chamber, and “it was hoped that politics of confrontation would end”. “Unfortunately, that did not happen. They [PTI] only had one purpose: to ensure that the talks do not succeed,” the premier said, adding that the opposition party demanded changes to things already settled upon. PM Shehbaz asserted that these protests and long marches affected the country’s economy and created hindrances in exports, imports and manufacturing. “We collectively improved the economy in 2.5 years and reached macroeconomic stability. Now is the time for it to flourish,” the premier added. “In September, our information technology exports, remittances and the country’s production improved,” he said. “If someone harms it, is it not equivalent to being an enemy of the country?” The premier stressed that putting the economy in shambles and the lives of people in danger will not be allowed. “The law will take its course,” he said. “I will still say: come to your senses. Will your actions harm the country or benefit it? … End your long march and protests. When you end them, we will surely sit down with you,” he said. Earlier in the same ceremony, Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi said, without naming anyone, that people had to see for themselves which public representatives were working for their welfare and which ones were engaging in “negative politics”. Tallal says talks conditional on PTI calling off march Separately, Minister of State for Interior Tallal Chaudhry also spoke about the resumption of talks, saying that it remained conditional upon PTI calling off its marches and protests. Addressing a press conference in Islamabad, he warned that constitutional and political measures were in place to respond to the PTI’s ongoing long march and held Khyber Pakhtunkhwa Chief Minister Sohail Afridi responsible for the breakdown in negotiations. “Political and constitutional measures are in place,” Chaudhry said. Minister of State for Interior Tallal Chaudhry speaks to media on Oct 6, 2026. — DawnNewsTV He added that the “wise” people part of the PTI’s delegation had tried to make the talks successful. Chaudhry further said that if the talks had succeeded, Pakistan would have had a united political front and the PTI would have gained “political space”. He added that a “hardening of the state” was now close, stressing that “enough softness has been shown”. “The state is like a mother, but it also has to act like a father at times,” Chaudhry said. “Constitutional options are under discussion, but the political option comes first,” he said. Commenting on the talks, Chaudhry told reporters that on the first day, Naqvi presented the government’s position regarding terrorism in KP, which included facts about the provincial government’s lack of involvement in the province’s affairs, budget and counterterrorism efforts. Chaudhry said the next day, the PTI delegation returned to Islamabad to continue talks after discussing the terms of the agreement with KP’s senior leadership in Peshawar. He said CM Afridi had previously reassured the Centre that the PTI delegation had the authority to reach an agreement on behalf of the provincial government. “We were assured that on terrorism, they [PTI] agreed 100 per cent on the federal government’s points,” Chaudhry said, adding that it was only then that Naqvi travelled to Lahore to PM Shehbaz and informed him that the PTI and the PML-N had agreed on the terrorism issue. “The prime minister said, ‘give as much political space as you can’,” Chaudhry told the media. According to him, PM Shehbaz told Naqvi that “parties’ political capital comes and goes”. Chaudhry said the premier further told Naqvi that when Pakistan was on the brink of financial default, strict measures reduced PML-N’s political capital, but they ensured that the country would not default. The second day of the talks started after the two sides had agreed on the issue of terrorism, Chaudhry said. “The win for us in the draft agreement was that we would be successful in bringing the PTI to the same page for eliminating terrorism,” he said. The draft was ready by 9pm on the second day of the talks, and Naqvi was getting ready to take it to President Asif Ali Zardari, according to the state minister. “Everything was fine,” he said, adding that some back and forth happened on further edits, but they were all agreed upon. “At the last minute, the opposition sat in a separate room for a while to consult with the KP chief minister. When they came out, they couldn’t look us in the eye and asked for permission to leave,” Chaudhry said. He added that the PTI delegation thanked the PML-N for patiently conducting the talks. The nation had agreed on the two National Action Plans (NAP) against terrorism, Chaudhry said, adding that the second plan was agreed upon during the PTI’s government under former prime minister Imran. He said that NAP was linked to “Pakistan’s Constitution, its needs, security, stability and Islamic teachings”. Citing Afridi’s statement that he wouldn’t allow a plan against the people of KP, Chaudhry questioned if Imran’s NAP was against the people of the province. Chaudhry claimed that KP was unsafe for common people and politicians alike; however, he noted that at the same time, the PTI’s leaders and workers were safe from threats in the same region. “The only one safe there is PTI,” he said, questioning, “Why do [terrorists] have a soft corner for you only?” On the possibility of talks resuming, Chaudhry said that any further talks were conditional upon the PTI calling off its marches and protests. “Don’t encourage terrorists. Instead, let’s kill them together,” Chaudhry further stated. Responding to a question about the PTI’s ongoing long march, he said, “Someone could not take over a country of 260 million people by bringing 50,000 to 100,000 people to the capital. “They are mistaken. Once their misunderstanding is cleared this time, a march won’t happen again in Pakistan,” he warned. Opp-govt dialogue failure Over the weekend, the government and opposition held two rounds of talks , which did not yield positive results, with counterterrorism policies and access to Imran emerging as two major sticking points. On Sunday, the PTI said it wanted immediate access to party chief Imran for consultations, and even agreed to forgo other demands in return for a meeting with Imran. However, the government declined to make access to Imran part of the proposed agreement, the opposition party claimed. Another deadlock was terrorism in KP. The federal government asked the KP government to support its counterterrorism measures and support emergency measures within 72 hours in the merged tribal districts, the PTI said. Instead, the PTI proposed that authorised representatives of the federal and KP governments meet within 72 hours to develop a clear, comprehensive and mutually agreed strategy for peace and counterterrorism, the statement added. The PTI said the health and medical treatment of Imran Khan was also raised as a matter of fundamental importance. Meanwhile, PTI leader Salman Akram Raja, who was a part of the opposition’s delegation, said the primary reason for the failure was disagreement on anti-terrorism actions in KP. Raja said the opposition stood firm on its principled position that anti-terrorism actions should be based on an agreement between the federal government and the KP government, and would be framed in consultation with stakeholders. After talks between the government and the opposition ended without headway, interior minister Naqvi on Sunday accused CM Afridi of “sabotaging” negotiations. On Sunday, Naqvi also held a meeting with KP Governor Faisal Karim Kundi to discuss the political and security situation amid speculations of ‘imminent’ governor’s rule in the province. A government source told Dawn that the government was seriously considering the imposition of the governor’s rule in KP. But Special Assistant to the Prime Minister on Political Affairs Rana Sanaullah said on Monday that a return to negotiations was possible if there was an assurance of positive progress by the opposition regarding counterterrorism efforts in KP. Speaking on Geo News ’ programme ‘Capital Talk’, he said that the federal government aimed to end terrorism in Pakistan, protect its borders and keep people safe. “The provincial government will have to play its role at any cost in this policy and operation,” he added. He said that both sides were still in contact, and said that if “better sense prevails” amongst the opposition and they could provide “assurance of some positive progress” in this regard, then they could sit down for more talks.

items.title: Attempted kidnap: FCT Police rescue suspect from jungle justice
items.description: By Kingsley Omonobi The FCT Police Command said its operatives on the 4th of October 2026 at approximately 02:46pm received a distress call reporting that an unidentified adult male was being assaulted by an angry mob over an alleged attempt to abduct a child. Following receipt of the report, police operatives from Kuje Division were immediately dispatched to the scene, where one Bashir Usman was rescued from an irate mob that was about to lynch him. Spokesperson of the command, SP Josephine Adeh, said, “Preliminary investigations revealed that the suspect was being assaulted by the mob over allegations that he attempted to abduct a five year old child in front of her residence in Angwan Lado, Kuje Area Council of the FCT. “The suspect has been taken into protective custody, while investigations into the alleged crime is being expanded to unravel the extent of his activities and apprehend any accomplices who may be involved. “The Commissioner of Police, FCT Police Command, CP Ahmed Muhammed Sanusi strongly discourages members of the public from taking the law into their own hands or engaging in jungle justice.” He said such acts are criminal and tantamount to murder under the law. The Command enjoined parents and guardians to remain vigilant and pay close attention to the safety and well-being of their children and wards. Members of the public are urged to promptly report suspicious persons or activities to the nearest Police station or through the Command’s emergency numbers: 08028940883, 08032003913. items.title: Crise d’eau en Guinée : Mohamed Kourouma explique la rareté de l’eau en bouteille
items.description: Depuis l’entrée en vigueur, le 21 septembre dernier, de l’interdiction de l’utilisation des sachets plastiques à usage unique, le marché guinéen fait face à une importante « crise » sur l’approvisionnement en eau conditionnée. Une situation que Mohamed Kourouma, PDG de la société Hamana, explique notamment par le déséquilibre entre la demande et les capacités actuelles de production des bouteilles d’eau. S’exprimant lors d’une conférence de presse tenue ce mardi 6 octobre, le patron de Hamana a d’abord salué l’adhésion de la population à la nouvelle mesure. Selon lui, la disparition rapide de l’eau conditionnée en sachet traduit une volonté des Guinéens de se conformer à la réglementation. « Il faut féliciter la population guinéenne. Depuis l'interdiction de l'utilisation des sachets plastiques à usage unique, l'eau en sachet a disparu en trois jours. Cela veut dire que le Guinéen a commencé à comprendre qu'il faut respecter la loi. C'est la loi qui est importante », a-t-il déclaré. Pour Mohamed Kourouma, la crise actuelle trouve son origine dans la structure même du marché de l’eau en Guinée. Avant l’interdiction, la consommation reposait très largement sur les sachets, tandis que les bouteilles occupaient une part beaucoup plus réduite. « En Guinée, ce sont les sachets et les bouteilles qui sont utilisées pour la consommation d'eau. Et c'est 85 % de la population qui utilisait l'eau en sachet et 15 % utilisaient les bouteilles d'eau », a-t-il expliqué. Avec la disparition des sachets, cette répartition a donc été brutalement bouleversée. Les capacités actuelles de production et de distribution des bouteilles ne permettent pas, selon le PDG de Hamana, de répondre immédiatement à l’ensemble de la demande. « Avec l'interdiction de l'utilisation des plastiques à usage unique, les sachets d'eau ont disparu. Maintenant les 15 % de bouteilles d'eau qui sont sur le marché ne suffisent pas à toute la population. C'est pour cela il y a eu une crise d'eau », a-t-il poursuivi. Face à cette nouvelle donne, l’enjeu consiste désormais à augmenter progressivement l’offre en bouteilles d’eau afin de compenser la disparition des sachets. Mais cette adaptation ne peut, selon Mohamed Kourouma, se faire du jour au lendemain. « Maintenant, pour produire 100 % de bouteilles d'eau, ça va prendre du temps. C'est la difficulté qu'il y a en ce moment. Il faut se dire la vérité », a-t-il reconnu. Le PDG de Hamana estime ainsi que la situation actuelle doit être comprise comme une période de transition consécutive à l’application de la nouvelle réglementation. Tout en reconnaissant les difficultés auxquelles les consommateurs sont confrontés, Mohamed Kourouma appelle à faire confiance aux autorités pour trouver une réponse à cette situation. « Maintenant je pense que l'État est là pour aider la population, il n'est pas là pour la fatiguer. L'État est en train d'étudier. Je pense qu'ils vont trouver la solution », a-t-il conclu. La crise actuelle met ainsi en évidence le défi posé par la transition entre un mode de consommation largement dépendant des sachets plastiques et un marché appelé désormais à s’adapter à une offre davantage orientée vers les bouteilles d’eau. items.title: Preuves recueillies sur les champs de bataille : le Sénégal plaide pour une chaîne judiciaire fiable
items.description: À l’ouverture, ce 6 octobre 2026 à Dakar, de l’atelier régional sur les preuves recueillies sur les champs de bataille en Afrique de l’Ouest, le ministre de la Justice, Garde des Sceaux, Maître Moussa Sarr, a appelé à mieux organiser le passage de la preuve du terrain militaire au prétoire. La rencontre réunit pendant trois jours magistrats, enquêteurs, experts et officiers de quatorze pays d’Afrique de l’Ouest et du voisinage. Faire de la preuve militaire un élément exploitable par la justice Pour le ministre, l’un des principaux défis réside dans la capacité à transformer les éléments recueillis lors des opérations militaires en preuves recevables devant les tribunaux. Téléphones, ordinateurs, documents, armes ou données biométriques peuvent être déterminants dans les procédures judiciaires, mais leur utilisation suppose des méthodes de collecte, de conservation et de transmission suffisamment rigoureuses. « Tout l’enjeu est là. Comment faire d’un élément saisi au cours d’une opération militaire une preuve recevable devant un tribunal ? Comment y parvenir sans rien céder des garanties du procès équitable ? », a résumé Maître Moussa Sarr. Il a identifié trois exigences majeures : lutter contre l’impunité, garantir l’admissibilité de la preuve et respecter les droits de l’homme. Une preuve doit notamment permettre d’établir son origine, son auteur, ses conditions de conservation et les modalités de sa transmission. La chaîne de la preuve au cœur des préoccupations Le ministre a insisté sur la nécessité d’une meilleure coordination entre militaires, enquêteurs et magistrats. La saisie, l’établissement du procès-verbal, la mise sous scellé, la remise aux enquêteurs, l’extraction des données numériques et leur authentification constituent, selon lui, une véritable chaîne dont chaque maillon doit être sécurisé. « Un dossier vaut ce que valent ses preuves », a-t-il rappelé, en soulignant que le lien entre les forces présentes sur le terrain et l’autorité judiciaire doit être organisé en amont du procès. Le ministre a également souligné les difficultés particulières liées aux informations classifiées, qui doivent être conciliées avec les droits de la défense et les exigences d’un procès équitable. Coopération régionale et respect des droits Face à une menace terroriste qui dépasse les frontières, Maître Moussa Sarr a plaidé pour une coopération judiciaire renforcée. Les procédures d’entraide doivent être rendues plus rapides afin de faciliter le partage des éléments de preuve entre États. Le respect des droits humains demeure, toutefois, une ligne rouge. « Une preuve obtenue au mépris de la dignité humaine n’a pas sa place dans un prétoire, quelle que soit la gravité des faits », a déclaré le ministre. Il a également rappelé que la coopération entre forces de défense et de sécurité et autorités judiciaires ne saurait remettre en cause l’indépendance du juge, qui apprécie librement les éléments qui lui sont soumis. Au terme des trois jours de travaux, le ministre attend des participants des solutions pratiques, adaptées aux différents systèmes juridiques et applicables rapidement, ainsi que la mise en place de relations de travail durables entre magistrats, enquêteurs, experts et militaires. C.G.D

items.title: N’Zérékoré : Zaly Propriété lance la collecte des déchets dans sept quartiers pour améliorer l’assainissement
items.description: Un nouveau dispositif de collecte et de gestion des déchets est désormais opérationnel dans la commune urbaine de N’Zérékoré. Le lancement officiel des activités de Zaly Propriété a eu lieu ce lundi 5 octobre 2026, au quartier Ossud, en présence des autorités communales et de plusieurs acteurs locaux. L’entreprise entend contribuer à l’amélioration du cadre de vie à travers la collecte régulière des ordures ménagères. Ses premières opérations concernent sept quartiers : Dorota 1, Dorota 2, Commercial, Boyéba, Zébela Topa, Nye et Mohomou. Selon Bakary Kaba, coordinateur de Zaly Propriété, le dispositif déployé comprend notamment cinq tricycles, un camion et une tractopelle, avec des équipes chargées d’assurer la collecte des déchets. Pour lui, la réussite du projet repose toutefois sur l’implication des populations. Les ménages sont invités à éviter les dépôts sauvages, à respecter les horaires de collecte et à s’acquitter de leur contribution conformément aux modalités d’abonnement. Présent à la cérémonie, le maire de N’Zérékoré, Germain Tavaguez Kolié, a salué l’arrivée de ce partenaire, estimant que la mairie ne peut, à elle seule, assurer l’assainissement de toute la ville. La commune entend accompagner Zaly Propriété, notamment en facilitant les relations entre l’entreprise et les ménages. La police communale devrait également contribuer au respect des engagements pris entre les parties. Le maire a par ailleurs insisté sur le suivi de l’acheminement des déchets jusqu’aux sites de dépôt, avant l’instauration progressive du tri sélectif. Il a également demandé à l’entreprise de signaler les zones encore confrontées aux dépôts sauvages afin de permettre à la mairie d’y mener des actions de sensibilisation. Pour Nagnouma Traoré, l’initiative constitue une satisfaction pour les habitants, qui espèrent voir leur environnement et leurs ménages davantage assainis. Avec ce lancement, la commune urbaine de N’Zérékoré mise ainsi sur un partenariat entre les autorités, les opérateurs d’assainissement et les citoyens pour améliorer durablement la gestion des déchets. items.title: Government to launch new legal frameworks on social protection and gender equity
items.description: The Ministry of Gender, Children and Social Protection will, on Wednesday, October 7, officially launch three major legal and regulatory instruments aimed at strengthening Ghana’s social protection system and advancing gender equity and inclusion. The instruments are the Social Protection Act, 2025 (Act 1148), the Social Protection Regulations, 2026 (L.I. 2521) and the Affirmative Action (Gender Equity) Regulations, 2026 (L.I. 2522). The launch, which will take place in Accra, will be held under the theme “Building an Inclusive, Equitable and Resilient Ghana: From Legislation to Impact.” According to the Ministry, the three instruments represent an important step towards strengthening Ghana’s legal and institutional framework for social protection and promoting greater gender equity and inclusion. The Social Protection Act, 2025 (Act 1148) provides the legal foundation for a coordinated national social protection system. The Act seeks to promote the well-being of people experiencing poverty, vulnerability and social or economic risks, while providing institutional arrangements to strengthen the coordination and delivery of social protection interventions. The Social Protection Regulations, 2026 (L.I. 2521) provide the regulatory framework for implementing the Act. The Affirmative Action (Gender Equity) Regulations, 2026 (L.I. 2522), meanwhile, provide the framework for implementing the Affirmative Action (Gender Equity) Act, 2024 (Act 1121) and advancing its objectives on gender equity and inclusion. The Ministry said the three legal instruments will collectively provide an important framework for strengthening coordination, accountability and implementation across social protection and gender equity interventions. They are also expected to clarify the responsibilities of institutions involved in implementing the various measures. The Ministry said the launch will provide an opportunity to deepen public understanding of the new legal and regulatory frameworks and highlight the importance of translating their provisions into practical outcomes for citizens. “The launch, under the theme ‘Building An Inclusive, Equitable and Resilient Ghana: From Legislation to Impact,’ highlights the need to translate laws into practical action that strengthens social protection delivery, promotes inclusion and creates greater opportunities for women and other disadvantaged groups,” the Ministry said. Vice President Prof. Naana Jane Opoku-Agyemang will officially launch the three legal instruments. Government institutions, development partners, civil society organisations, social protection programme stakeholders, the private sector and traditional leaders are expected to participate in the event. The Ministry said the launch is intended to reinforce the need for effective implementation of the new frameworks to ensure that the legal provisions translate into stronger social protection delivery, greater inclusion and increased opportunities for women and other disadvantaged groups.

items.title: ¿Qué pasará con HBO Max y SkyShowtime tras la fusión de Warner y Paramount en Skydance?
items.description: Hollywood está cambiando. Este martes, y tras meses de negociaciones, batallas judiciales y recriminaciones políticas, se ha cerrado uno de los mayores capítulos empresariales de la historia del entretenimiento: dos de los estudios centenarios del cine se fusionan haciendo más pequeña la industria. Warner Discovery, fundado en 1923, y Paramount Skydance, de 1912, (y que ya venían de sus propias uniones) serán una única compañía en manos del magnate David Ellison y la marca Skydance. En plena época de reducción del mercado, esto supone una transformación para los creativos, las series y películas y también para el cliente que ve sus obras en casa. ¿Qué significa este giro para HBO Max y SkyShowtime, así como para el resto de la industria televisiva? items.description: By Ugochukwu Alaribe UMUAHIA – Candidate of the All Progressives Congress ,APC, for the Abia South Senatorial zone in the 2027 general election,Prince Paul Ikonne, has said that the commercial city of Aba in Abia State needs deliberate and sustained backing from the federal government to support its businesses to compete and succeed on the global economic stage. Speaking at the 10th Anniversary celebration of Umuaba Connect group,in Aba, Ikonne lauded the group’s age-long commitment to upholding the vision of the founding fathers of the city of Aba. He added that the city’s immense creative and entrepreneurial energy must be translated into sustainable economic value for greater growth and development. The Umuaba Connect hailed Ikonne’s senatorial ambition for the upcoming election, describing him as a genuine Aba man and a proven entrepreneur whose visible footprints in local business development serve as a reliable guarantee of his capacity to deliver effective representation at the National Assembly. Ikonne noted that the city already possesses the core ingredients for global success and commended the innate capabilities of the people. He said;”Aba has never lacked talent, ingenuity or resilience. From manufacturing and fashion to trade, technology and entrepreneurship. Our people continue to demonstrate what is possible when skill meets determination.” The senatorial hopeful noted that while the city’s industrious reputation is widely acknowledged, more commitment should be made to sustain its growth to empower the massive business ecosystem. “What Aba needs now is more than recognition. It needs deliberate attention from the federal government, strategic support and stronger institutional backing to help its businesses compete and succeed on a bigger stage.” Outlining his vision for the district and what he considers a collective duty for leadership in the region, Ikonne disclosed a three-pronged responsibility focused on advocacy, business environment optimization, and youth empowerment. “My responsibility is clear: To champion the recognition Aba deserves at the national stage, to help create an environment where businesses can thrive through the sponsorship and support of the right legislations and policies, to ensure that the creativity and hard work of our people translate into real economic value, sustainable businesses and meaningful opportunities for the next generation, and most importantly attract the needed federal government support.” He congratulated Umuaba Connect on reaching its milestone anniversary and tasked the members to remain steadfast in their vision for the transformation of the city. “Congratulations to Umuaba Connect on 10 years of impact and community building. The fire is already burning. Our duty is to keep it burning brighter.” The post Aba needs FG’s backing to compete on global business stage – Ikonne appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: FG orders CCECC to rebuild Abuja airport’s second runway
items.description: By Dickson Omobola The Federal Government has ordered the China Civil Engineering Construction Corporation, CCECC, to resume work on the second runway at the Nnamdi Azikiwe International Airport, Abuja. Minister of Aviation and Aerospace Development, Mr Festus Keyamo, disclosed this, saying that after delaying the project for nearly 20 years, it would now cost nearly N400 billion. Speaking in Lagos at the 67th anniversary of Aero Contractors, Keyamo said: “The President has also approved that CCECC goes back to Abuja and begins the rebuilding of the second runway. Why couldn’t we build the second runway all along? Don’t forget that this controversy (second runway) started during Obasanjo’s tenure. I remember vividly (I didn’t know I was going to come to the aviation sector, but I followed the debate) that the National Assembly at that time said because N45 billion was too much to do the second runway. “So, the committee on aviation…, we could not raise N45 billion at that time to do the second runway. 15 years or nearly 20 years later, it’s now costing us nearly N400 billion. That is the danger in delaying the building of infrastructure because the prices will go up every day.” On Aero Contractors’ 67th anniversary, he said the airline was an example of the saying that tough times do not last, but tough people do. He said: “This is the story of Aero Contractors. From 1969 to where we are today, Aero Contractors has survived to this point. In those years, we have witnessed the highest rate of mortality of airlines in Africa and Nigeria. But in the midst of all this, Aero Contractors survived in Nigeria. “The last time I called for the report from the Nigeria Civil Authority, NCAA, we had 100 airlines that have gone under in Nigeria. That is how high the mortality rate has been. Many of them, including Okada, Chanchangi and Concord Airlines. Here we are today celebrating Aero Contractors. This is the pride of Nigeria. This is a story of the Nigerian spirit, and it is what we should all be celebrating as a country and nation.” The post FG orders CCECC to rebuild Abuja airport’s second runway appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Le Fongip primé au Forum mondial sur le financement des femmes entrepreneures à Paris
items.description: Le Fonds de Garantie des Investissements Prioritaires (FONGIP) a été distingué à Paris pour ses actions en faveur de l’accès des femmes entrepreneures au financement. Représenté par son Secrétaire général, M. Abdoulaye Diassé, le FONGIP a participé, ce 1er et 2 octobre 2026, au Forum mondial sur le Code de financement pour les femmes entrepreneures, organisé au Centre de conférence de l’OCDE à Paris par Women Entrepreneurs Finance Initiative (We-Fi), une initiative mondiale pilotée par la Banque mondiale. Cette rencontre réunit plus de 500 acteurs issus notamment des institutions multilatérales, banques centrales, régulateurs financiers, fournisseurs de services financiers et organismes spécialisés dans les données. M. Abdoulaye Diassé a pris part aux discussions de haut niveau consacrées à la transformation des engagements en résultats durables et mesurables pour les femmes entrepreneures, au renforcement des systèmes de données et à la mise en place de mécanismes incitatifs destinés à améliorer le financement des entreprises dirigées par des femmes. Point fort de cette participation : le FONGIP a reçu le WE Finance Code Award, au nom du Sénégal, en reconnaissance de ses actions et mesures incitatives en faveur du financement des femmes entrepreneures. Cette distinction vient ainsi mettre en lumière l’engagement du Sénégal et du FONGIP dans la promotion de l’inclusion financière et le développement de solutions adaptées aux besoins des femmes entrepreneures.

items.title: Difficult terrain stalls evacuation of victims 24 hours after Ondo plane crash
items.description: By Dayo Johnson, Akure AKURE — Evacuation of victims of the Nigerian Air Force aircraft crash in Igbokoda, headquarters of Ilaje Local Government Area of Ondo State, has been stalled by the swampy and inaccessible terrain where the aircraft went down. Twenty-four hours after the incident, emergency responders were still battling to retrieve the wreckage and remains of those on board as of Tuesday morning. The ATR-42 aircraft, which crashed on Monday morning, was said to be deeply submerged in the swamp, making rescue operations extremely difficult. Sources at the scene said thick mangroves and murky waters had hampered access to the exact location of the wreckage. Journalists were denied access to the crash site, located about 500 metres east of the Naval Base, which had been cordoned off. Some television journalists were reportedly arrested by Navy authorities for allegedly accessing the site without clearance. In an interview, the state Commissioner of Police, Felix Ohagwu, described the terrain as very challenging. Ohagwu said: “What happened yesterday was quite unfortunate. It is a very difficult terrain — the creeks, mangroves. Accessing the site of the crash was not easy. I had to use a smaller boat, a canoe, to access it. “I thank the OCA, Marine, and the DPO, Igbokoda, who have been on ground since yesterday, giving us support. “For now, the recovery of the wreckage is still in progress. More technical support is being awaited. “Most of the scene has been calmed down. We are still expecting a bigger machine to be able to pull the wreckage from the water.” The police commissioner said the command was awaiting a response from the National Emergency Management Agency, NEMA, and other relevant agencies to deploy heavy equipment needed to pull the aircraft from the swamp. Addressing newsmen in Igbokoda, the state Commissioner for Health, Dr Banji Ajaka, said he had been in the forest alongside the Commanding Officer of the Forward Operating Base, FOB, Igbokoda, supervising the operation. Ajaka said personnel and ambulances from hospitals in Ilaje and Okitipupa Local Government Areas had been deployed on the directive of Governor Lucky Aiyedatiwa. According to him, “I have been in the forest with the CO, FOB Igbokoda, for search and rescue operations. “I have deployed personnel and ambulances from all hospitals in Ilaje and Okitipupa LGAs as directed by Mr Governor. The site is about 500 metres east of the Naval Base. People are just videoing and posting all manner of information far away from the site. “I was at the place till around 11 p.m. with local divers and the CO and his men.” Ajaka described the incident as a national tragedy that should not be politicised and urged members of the public to avoid spreading unverified information. “This is a national disaster that we shouldn’t play politics with. Please, let’s tarry and wait for verified information,” he said. He added that swamp buggies and other rescue equipment would be deployed to continue the operation early Wednesday. The commissioner commended the Commanding Officer of FOB Igbokoda, his men, local divers and medical personnel from the State Specialist Hospital, Okitipupa, General Hospital, Igbokoda, and Comprehensive Health Centre, Igbokoda, for their efforts. Ajaka prayed that “May we not experience this type of monumental loss again in this country.” The post Difficult terrain stalls evacuation of victims 24 hours after Ondo plane crash appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: CSA Ghana opens NCSAM 2026 with call for stronger cybersecurity collaboration
items.description: … National Cyber Security Awareness Month 2026 opens under theme focused on securing the digital finance ecosystem The Cyber Security Authority (CSA) has marked its fifth anniversary with a call for stronger collaboration across Ghana’s digital finance ecosystem, urging institutions to move beyond broad commitments to information-sharing and make coordinated cyber defence part of their daily operations.The call was made at the official opening of the 2026 National Cyber Security Awareness Month (NCSAM) at the Cedi Conference Centre, University of Ghana, under the theme ‘Securing Ghana’s Digital Finance Ecosystem: Building Trust Through Collaboration and Cyber Resilience’. Opening the month-long campaign, the Director-General of the CSA, Mr. Divine Selase Agbeti, said Ghana’s rapid digital transformation had created significant opportunities for economic growth, financial inclusion and innovation, but had also expanded the opportunities available to cybercriminals. “Ghana has made a deliberate choice to embrace digital transformation. We must now make an equally deliberate choice to secure it,” Mr. Agbeti said. He stressed that protecting the country’s digital economy could not be left to any single institution, calling for a coordinated response among government, regulators, financial institutions, fintechs, telecommunications companies, technology firms, law enforcement agencies and cybersecurity service providers. “The government cannot do it alone. The Cyber Security Authority cannot do it alone. Banks cannot do it alone. Fintechs cannot do it alone. Telecommunications companies cannot do it alone. Cybersecurity is a team sport and Ghana must play as one team,” he said. Mr. Agbeti called on financial institutions to share actionable threat intelligence, telecommunications companies to deepen cooperation with banks and fintechs, and regulators, technology companies, law enforcement agencies and cybersecurity service providers to exchange information quickly enough to disrupt attacks before they result in financial losses. Rising cyber threats The urgency of the call is reflected in data from the national Computer Emergency Response Team (CERT), coordinated by the CSA, which recorded 3,876 cybersecurity incidents between January and July 2026. Online fraud accounted for approximately 47 percent of the reported incidents. Mr. Agbeti said the impact of cybercrime extended beyond the immediate financial loss suffered by victims, with repeated incidents capable of undermining public confidence in digital services. “When a Ghanaian loses money to cyber fraud, we lose more than money. We lose confidence,” he said, noting that declining confidence in digital platforms could affect financial inclusion, electronic commerce, innovation and the wider digital transformation agenda. The Director-General also stressed that cyber risk must be treated as a business and national security issue rather than solely as a technology concern. “Cybersecurity must not remain buried somewhere in the technology department. Cyber risk is business risk,” he said, urging boards, chief executives and senior leaders to take direct ownership of cyber risk and regularly assess their organisations’ preparedness. Mr Divine Selase Agbeti, Director General, Cyber Security Authority delivers the welcome address at the official opening of the Cyber Security Awareness Month (NCSAM) 2026 “How quickly can we detect an intrusion? How quickly can we contain it? If our systems fail tonight, can we continue operating tomorrow morning? Do we know which third parties have access to our critical systems and data? And when the attack eventually comes, have we practised our response, or are we simply hoping our technology will save us?” he asked. Strengthening collective defence The opening brought together representatives of the Ministry of Communication, Digital Technology and Innovations, Ministry of the Interior, Ministry of Tourism, Culture and Creative Arts, Bank of Ghana and University of Ghana, alongside stakeholders from industry, academia and civil society. Speaking on behalf of the Governor of the Bank of Ghana, Dr. Johnson Pandit Asiama, the Head of Cyber and Information Security, Mr. Daniel Sowah Klu, said the central bank had revised its Cyber and Information Security Directive, established a digital forensic laboratory to support investigations and prosecutions, and was developing an industry-wide fraud intelligence hub. The Deputy Minister for Communication, Digital Technology and Innovations, Hon. Mohammed Adams Sukparu, representing the Minister, Hon. Samuel Nartey George, announced plans for a digital fraud monitoring system to strengthen the detection, prevention and response to fraudulent activities across digital platforms. The Deputy Minister for the Interior, Hon. Ebenezer Okletey Terlabi, representing the Minister, Hon. Muntaka Mohammed-Mubarak, said the digital environment had become an increasingly important component of Ghana’s national security landscape and reaffirmed the Ministry’s commitment to strengthening law enforcement capacity to trace digital evidence and pursue offenders across borders. The University of Ghana, in remarks delivered on behalf of the Vice-Chancellor, Professor Nana Aba Appiah Amfo, pledged continued support through cybersecurity research, professional training and the development of skilled cybersecurity professionals. The Minister for Tourism, Culture and Creative Arts, Hon. Abla Dzifa Gomashie, highlighted the potential impact of cyber fraud targeting visitors on Ghana’s reputation and tourism sector. The ceremony also featured the unveiling of a commemorative digital plaque marking the CSA’s fifth anniversary. Mr. Agbeti said the Authority would continue working with law enforcement, intelligence, regulatory and international partners to strengthen Ghana’s ability to identify, investigate and disrupt cyber-enabled crime. “Technology may allow criminals to cross borders. It does not place them beyond accountability,” he said. Public vigilance remains critical The CSA reminded citizens that cybersecurity begins with individual action and urged the public to pause before clicking links in messages or emails; verify details before transferring money; protect passwords and one-time authentication codes; and question unexpected requests for money, even when the voice, message or image appears to come from someone they know. The Authority also warned that advances in artificial intelligence are making it increasingly difficult to rely solely on visual or audio cues when verifying identities. “In the age of artificial intelligence, seeing is no longer necessarily believing. Verification must become a habit,” Mr. Agbeti said. Members of the public can report cybersecurity incidents and cybercrime to the CSA by calling or texting 292, or by email at report@csa.gov.gh . Throughout October, the Authority will work with partners across the financial, telecommunications, public and academic sectors to deliver cybersecurity awareness activities aimed at promoting safer digital practices and strengthening resilience nationwide. As the CSA enters its sixth year, Mr. Agbeti called for NCSAM 2026 to serve as a catalyst for deeper and more practical collaboration. “Let us secure every transaction. Let us strengthen every institution. Let us protect every citizen. And together, let us build a digital Ghana that our people can trust,” he said.

items.title: Israël aurait envisagé d’abattre l’avion de Flydubai pour éviter un nouveau 11-Septembre
items.description: Israel aurait ete pret a abattre un avion de la compagnie Flydubai apres l'agression du commandant de bord, bien qu'il y ait eu plus de 150 citoyens israeliens a bord, a rapporte CBS News le 5 octobre, citant deux sources israeliennes. Selon ces sources, cette decision s'inscrirait dans un protocole d'intervention mis au point de longue date a Tel Aviv pour prevenir des attentats similaires a ceux du 11 septembre. Apres que l'avion a brusquement perdu environ 4 200 metres d'altitude, l'armee de l'air israelienne a tente de contacter le poste de pilotage. Faute de reponse, une commission speciale a ete rapidement convoquee et un poste de commandement mis en place, les autorites ayant mobilise des chasseurs et ferme l'espace aerien du pays. Les chasseurs ont ensuite ete rappeles lorsqu'il est apparu que l'avion, a environ 640 km d'Israel, avait mis le cap sur l'Arabie saoudite, ou les autorites saoudiennes avaient elles-memes fait decoller des chasseurs. Neanmoins, la situation aurait pu prendre une tout autre tournure si l'avion de Flydubai s'etait approche a une certaine distance d'Israel. Selon des sources de CBS News, dans un tel scenario, Tel Aviv aurait envoye des chasseurs dans l'espace aerien jordanien pour evaluer la situation. Les pilotes des chasseurs auraient alors dû inspecter le cockpit et tenter d'etablir un contact visuel avec le pilote de l'avion. Ils auraient ensuite dû evaluer l'etat des passagers et, en cas de panique, transmettre les informations recueillies au commandement de l'armee de l'air et a une commission speciale. En cas de detournement d'un avion, la commission prendrait contact avec le ministre de la Defense et le Premier ministre. Le protocole prevoit d'abattre en vol un avion se dirigeant vers Israel s'il represente une menace, mais seul le chef du gouvernement est habilite a prendre une telle decision. Cependant, les sources de la chaîne ont assure que la destruction d'un avion de ligne constituerait un moindre mal par rapport a la mort de centaines de personnes si cet appareil venait a percuter les tours Azrieli (un centre commercial de Tel Aviv), un aeroport ou tout autre site d'importance strategique. Un attentat dû a la negligence, qui a failli tourner au drame Le 30 septembre, un avion de Flydubai, qui assurait la liaison entre Dubaï et Tel Aviv, a soudainement change de cap et a procede a un atterrissage d'urgence a Tabuk. La cause en etait une bagarre entre le pilote et son copilote, Hamam al-Hammami, un citoyen omanais de 29 ans. Selon l'enquete, ce dernier est soupconne d'avoir agresse le commandant de bord, puis d'avoir tente de prendre le controle de l'appareil. Cette tentative de detournement, que le parquet des emirats arabes unis a depuis qualifiee d'acte terroriste, n'a pas abouti : l'agresseur a ete arrete par l'equipage et les passagers de l'avion. Quelques jours plus tard, les medias ont revele que Hamam al-Hammami avait suivi une formation au sein de la compagnie aerienne Oman Air, mais qu'il avait par la suite ete ecarte du cursus de pilotage en raison de craintes liees a ses opinions radicales. Le Wall Street Journal a indique que ce ressortissant omanais n'aurait pas dû effectuer de vols a destination d'Israel, car il est interdit aux pilotes originaires de pays n'entretenant pas de relations diplomatiques avec Tel Aviv de s'y rendre. Toujours selon le journal americain, Flydubai a transmis aux autorites israeliennes la liste des passagers et des membres d'equipage de ce vol, enregistree dans une base de donnees creee en 2023, notamment pour prevenir le terrorisme. Le ministere israelien des Transports a toutefois declare ne pas savoir qu'il avait acces a cette base de donnees. De plus, Flydubai pourrait elle-meme avoir fait preuve de negligence. Le Wall Street Journal a souligne que, lorsque la compagnie aerienne a embauche le copilote en fevrier dernier, elle a verifie son casier judiciaire, mais n'a pas contacte son ancien employeur pour evaluer son parcours professionnel.

items.title: Inondations : le gouvernement annonce des mesures et mobilise 921 milliards FCFA pour une réponse structurelle
items.description: Face aux fortes pluies enregistrées ces derniers jours et à la persistance du risque d’inondation, le gouvernement a renforcé son dispositif de réponse. Réuni en urgence lundi à la Primature, le Premier ministre Ahmadou Alhaminou M. Lo a arrêté plusieurs mesures destinées à secourir les sinistrés, préserver la mobilité et anticiper de nouvelles perturbations. Un plan d’urgence et une veille permanente Après avoir réuni les ministères et services concernés, le chef du gouvernement a annoncé le déclenchement du Plan d’urgence régional de Dakar, afin d’assurer une surveillance permanente de l’évolution de la situation. Cette décision intervient alors que de nouvelles précipitations sont annoncées dans les prochains jours. Un Comité de veille a également été institué aux côtés de l’état-major chargé de la gestion des intempéries. Plusieurs zones sensibles ont été identifiées, notamment les autoroutes, l’hôpital Philippe Maguilen Senghor et la zone de captage. Le gouvernement entend anticiper les éventuelles perturbations de l’approvisionnement en eau et en électricité. Des opérations de dégagement sont par ailleurs engagées dans les secteurs où les eaux entravent la circulation. Le dispositif prévoit aussi une meilleure information des populations à travers un système d’alerte. Secours aux sinistrés et rentrée scolaire sous surveillance Sur le volet social, le ministère chargé de la Famille et des Solidarités a reçu instruction d’apporter une assistance immédiate aux populations affectées. Des distributions d’eau et de denrées alimentaires sont prévues pour les personnes les plus durement touchées. Des moyens financiers doivent également être mobilisés pour les interventions d’urgence. La rentrée scolaire, prévue le 8 octobre pour les élèves, fait également l’objet d’une évaluation particulière à Dakar. Le ministre de l’Éducation nationale doit examiner l’état des établissements et des zones affectées. Si les conditions ne permettent pas une reprise normale des cours, un report pourra être proposé. Le gouvernement a, par ailleurs, réaffirmé sa compassion aux familles endeuillées et son soutien aux populations victimes des intempéries. Le Premier ministre s’est notamment rendu sur des sites touchés dans la banlieue dakaroise pour constater la situation et échanger avec les populations. Au-delà de l’urgence, une réponse structurelle Au-delà des interventions immédiates, l’exécutif entend inscrire la lutte contre les inondations dans une perspective de long terme. Le gouvernement a annoncé la mise en œuvre d’un programme national de lutte contre les inondations doté de 921 milliards de francs CFA, présenté comme une réponse structurelle à la récurrence du phénomène. La stratégie gouvernementale se déploie ainsi sur deux fronts : répondre sans délai aux conséquences des fortes pluies et renforcer, dans la durée, les dispositifs destinés à réduire la vulnérabilité des populations et des infrastructures face aux inondations. C.G.D

items.title: Yellow Fever deaths in Sissala East worrying – MP
items.description: Member of Parliament for Sissala East, Mohammed Issah Bataglia, has expressed concern over reported deaths linked to a Yellow Fever outbreak in parts of the municipality. The MP said the situation is worrying, following reports from community leaders that seven residents have died, with children and young people reportedly among those affected. Speaking in an interview on the Joy FM Midday News on Tuesday, October 6, Mr Issa Bataglia said he immediately contacted the Sissala East Municipal Health Directorate after receiving a report from the chief of one of the affected communities. “It’s quite worrying because I got a report from the chief of this place, informing me of the fact that they have lost most of their people.” He said he subsequently sought clarification from the Municipal Health Director to determine whether the situation had come to the attention of health authorities and what could be responsible for the reported deaths. “I quickly had to ask the municipal director whether that has come to their attention, or what might be the cause.” The MP said he also sought information on whether additional public education was needed to help residents understand and respond to the situation. His comments come amid reports of at least seven deaths in the municipality, with the affected communities calling for urgent intervention from health authorities.

items.title: PPS : opposition ou participation, un choix sous conditions
items.description: Réuni en session extraordinaire ce mardi, le comité central du Parti du progrès et du socialisme (PPS) examine deux options après les législatives du 23 septembre : rejoindre la prochaine majorité ou siéger dans l'opposition. Le bureau politique, qui n'a pas arrêté de choix, demande à l'instance un mandat pour gérer la prochaine étape. Présenté devant le comité central par le secrétaire général, Nabil Benabdallah, au nom du bureau politique, le rapport qualifie la décision de difficile. Le parti dit avoir pour habitude de ne pas précipiter ses choix importants, et sa décision devra rester guidée, en amont comme en aval, par l'intérêt du pays et du peuple ainsi que par la préservation de son unité, de sa cohésion et de sa force. Le bureau politique s'est réuni à cinq reprises en une semaine, la première réunion ayant eu lieu dès le 24 septembre pour une évaluation préliminaire du scrutin. Les discussions, marquées au départ par d'importantes divergences, ont rapproché les points de vue, ce que le rapport attribue notamment aux réponses rassurantes des interlocuteurs du parti. L'opposition est présentée comme une option ouverte à la discussion, qui peut avoir ses justifications et sa pertinence. La participation au gouvernement, jugée difficile, interroge le parti sur les rôles qu'il pourrait y jouer, au regard de l'ampleur des défis, du processus de réformes et des attentes immenses de la population. Sur le scrutin, le PPS souligne que la très faible participation a pesé lourdement sur les résultats, en particulier les siens, le parti comptant sur un vote politique massif des catégories populaires et moyennes. Selon le rapport, une grande partie de ces électeurs attachés à la démocratie, aux libertés et à la justice, ainsi qu'au camp de la gauche et de la modernité, n'a pas voté : plus de 11 millions de personnes ne sont pas inscrites sur les listes électorales, et environ 62 % des inscrits, soit près de 10 millions, ne se sont pas rendus aux urnes. Le parti rappelle aussi qu'environ deux millions d'électeurs ont été retirés des listes sans information préalable ni invitation à se réinscrire. Le rapport situe le scrutin dans un climat de colère populaire et de profond mécontentement à l'égard du gouvernement sortant, dont le bilan est jugé marqué par le service d'intérêts oligarchiques, la corruption, les conflits d'intérêts, la cherté de la vie, la dégradation du pouvoir d'achat et l'aggravation du chômage. Il estime que ce bilan a nourri la désaffection et la perte de confiance. La préparation des élections s'est, selon lui, déroulée sans mesures d'apaisement politique, pourtant réclamées à maintes reprises par le parti. Le PPS relève que les partis de la majorité sortante arrivent en tête, tout en jugeant que ces résultats doivent être lus à la lumière de la faible participation et de la perte de la première place par le parti qui dominait cette majorité. Il salue la non-intervention des autorités, avant comme pendant la campagne, qu'il juge un progrès important par rapport aux scrutins précédents. Il dénonce en revanche l'usage visible de moyens financiers considérables par certains candidats, dépassant très largement le plafond légal, ainsi que le recours à des pratiques corrompues pour influencer les électeurs. Le retard dans l'annonce des résultats a suscité des interrogations, et la non-remise des procès-verbaux dans plusieurs circonscriptions, jusqu'à tard dans la nuit, voire aux premières heures du matin, est jugée inacceptable et contraire à la loi, qui impose une remise immédiate. © Mounir Mehimdate Sur son propre résultat, le parti met en avant plusieurs mois de préparation et cinq ans d'opposition au gouvernement sortant. Il a couvert l'ensemble des circonscriptions législatives locales et régionales (92/92 et 12/12), avec un taux de renouvellement supérieur à 80 %. Parmi ses candidats, 72 % détenaient des diplômes universitaires supérieurs, neuf avaient moins de 35 ans et sept femmes conduisaient des listes dans des circonscriptions locales. Il regrette que son programme, présenté à la presse le 2 septembre, n'ait pas joué de rôle central dans le débat public ni dans les comportements électoraux. Ses résultats, qui traduisent selon lui une véritable capacité de résistance, ne sont pas à la hauteur de ses attentes, et la direction nationale les analysera pour en tirer les enseignements, sans que le parti renonce à son combat pour son projet de société. Le rapport évoque ensuite la nomination par le Roi, conformément à la Constitution, de Fatima Zahra El Mansouri, coordinatrice nationale de la direction collégiale du Parti Authenticité et Modernité (PAM), à la tête du gouvernement chargé d'être formé, après la victoire de sa formation. Le PPS la félicite et souligne la portée symbolique de la désignation, pour la première fois, d'une femme à ce poste, tout en estimant que l'enjeu dépasse cette dimension. Il appelle à un Parlement et à un gouvernement à la hauteur des défis, et à une classe politique qui entende les signaux qu'il juge à ne pas sous-estimer : les événements liés à la migration vers le préside occupé de Sebta, le mouvement « Gen Z » et l'abstention électorale, qu'il relie à la colère et au recul de la confiance. Lors de la rencontre d'une délégation du parti avec la cheffe du gouvernement désignée, le PPS affirme avoir mis en avant d'abord la restauration de la confiance et de la crédibilité du champ politique, par le renforcement de la démocratie, des libertés et des droits et par un apaisement politique. Il évoque, « par le moyen approprié », la libération des jeunes du mouvement « Gen Z » et de tout autre mouvement pacifique. Il réclame aussi l'activation des institutions prévues par la Constitution, la poursuite du processus d'égalité, notamment par l'adoption de la nouvelle réforme du Code de la famille, et la rupture avec la corruption, le clientélisme et les conflits d'intérêts. Sur le plan économique et social, le parti cite la souveraineté économique, l'industrialisation, la correction des insuffisances de la politique agricole, ainsi que l’emploi, la formation et l'éducation des jeunes. Il met aussi sur la table l'inflation et la cherté des prix, la généralisation effective de la protection sociale, l'amélioration des revenus, les retraites et pensions, l'indice et les dysfonctionnements de l'aide sociale directe. Il insiste enfin sur l'hôpital public, l'école publique et l'université publique. Au fil des consultations, le PPS dit avoir constaté un accueil positif de ces questions et d'autres points de convergence, au premier rang desquels la centralité de la question sociale, face à la dégradation du pouvoir d'achat. Il estime que la situation exige des mesures fortes, concrètes, urgentes et à effet direct sur le quotidien des citoyens, en ville comme à la campagne, en particulier pour les catégories vulnérables et la classe moyenne, ainsi que des réformes qui placent l'humain au cœur des politiques publiques et réduisent la pauvreté, la précarité et les inégalités sociales et territoriales. © Mounir Mehimdate Le programme gouvernemental ne devrait pas, selon lui, se limiter à un accord entre les composantes de la majorité, mais constituer un véritable contrat entre le gouvernement et l'ensemble des citoyens. Le PPS fait état d'échanges marqués par la confiance et d'une volonté de bâtir une orientation réformatrice nouvelle et commune. Le rapport rappelle que le comité central, parlement du parti et instance décisionnelle suprême entre deux congrès, est l'espace légitime pour débattre de ces questions et trancher. Les membres sont appelés à un débat libre, serein, approfondi et responsable, à l'image de celui du bureau politique. Des évolutions rapides sont attendues, liées aux orientations programmatiques de tout futur gouvernement, aux formations qui pourraient le composer et à la force réformatrice qu'il pourrait porter. Pour gérer cette période, le bureau politique demande donc au comité central de lui déléguer la gestion de la prochaine étape, sur la base d'un engagement qui place, au début comme à la fin, l'intérêt de la patrie et du peuple, ainsi que la préservation de l'unité, de la cohésion et de la force du parti. The post PPS : opposition ou participation, un choix sous conditions appeared first on Hespress Français - Actualités du Maroc .

items.title: UE : les sans-papiers désormais expulsables vers des pays tiers
items.description: Entre en vigueur le 2 octobre, le nouveau reglement europeen encadre les procedures d'eloignement force des etrangers sous le coup d'une obligation de quitter le territoire d'un etat membre. Les ressortissants algeriens en situation irreguliere sont notamment concernes par ces dispositions. Le texte permet de transferer certaines personnes expulsables vers des centres de retention, designes comme des « hubs retour », situes dans des pays tiers. Ces structures pourront etre etablies dans des pays respectant les normes internationales en matiere de droits de l'homme, dont le principe de non-refoulement. Les mineurs non accompagnes sont exclus de ce dispositif, tandis que les familles avec enfants pourraient etre concernees. Les personnes visees pourront etre soumises a des mesures de retention prolongees et a des interdictions d'entree sur le territoire europeen pouvant atteindre dix ans, voire 20 ans dans certains cas. Les etats membres pourront aussi reconnaître les decisions d'eloignement prises par leurs homologues, un mecanisme qui pourrait devenir obligatoire dans trois ans. Le reglement instaure par ailleurs des sanctions pour les personnes refusant de quitter le territoire ou ne cooperant pas avec les autorites. Elles peuvent prendre la forme d'une reduction des allocations, d'amendes ou, lorsque le droit national le prevoit, de sanctions penales. Autre changement : les recours contre les decisions d'eloignement ne seront plus automatiquement suspensifs. Une expulsion pourra ainsi avoir lieu malgre l'introduction d'un recours, sous certaines conditions. Les autorites seront aussi habilitees a fouiller les personnes et leurs biens, et saisir certains effets personnels et appareils electroniques. Le nouveau dispositif est conteste par des associations de defense des migrants. Chiara Catelli, de l'ONG belge Plateforme pour la cooperation internationale sur les migrants sans papiers (PICUM), estime qu'il risque d'intensifier les detentions et les expulsions et de renforcer la crainte des personnes sans papiers de solliciter les services publics ou une protection.

items.title: PAC flags GH¢5.2bn financial irregularities in 2025 audit report
items.description: Parliament’s Public Accounts Committee has raised concerns over financial irregularities amounting to GH¢5.2 billion, including GH¢4.8 billion in tax infractions identified in the 2025 audit report. Speaking at the Public Accounts Committee on October 6, Chairperson of Parliament’s Public Accounts Committee (PAC), Abena Osei-Asare, said the scale of the tax-related irregularities requires the Committee to establish what action has been taken by the relevant tax authorities. “We see a reported financial irregularity of five point two billion. But the most alarming thing is the tax infraction of four point eight billion.” She said the Committee will seek answers on how the tax authorities have responded to the findings and whether measures have been taken to remedy the situation. “And so we will seek to find answers and see how best our tax authorities have been able to remedy this situation.” The Committee is also raising concerns over the recurrence of similar audit findings involving public institutions from year to year. Ms Osei Asare said repeated findings involving the same institutions suggest that previous audit recommendations may not have resulted in sufficient corrective action. “A legitimate concern of the Ghanaian public is that many audit findings appear year after year.” She said when the same institution is repeatedly cited for the same control failure, the issue goes beyond the audit finding itself. “If the same institution is cited repeatedly for the same control failure, then we are no longer dealing with just audit findings, we are dealing with a failure to learn.” According to her, repeated infractions point to a failure by some ministries, departments and agencies to adequately address weaknesses identified in previous audits. “If it happens repeatedly, then we are no longer dealing with audit findings, but the ministries, departments or agencies’ failure to learn.” Ms Osei Asare said the Committee intends to adopt a different approach in its engagements with institutions cited in audit reports. She explained that institutions appearing before the Committee should be prepared to demonstrate what has changed as a result of previous audit findings. “So that is what auditees should be telling us. What changed or what has changed as a result of the audit?”
