items.title: Miners’ deaths: Panel finds ‘elements of institutional gaps, overzealousness’
items.description: …Seeks 2-week extension, cites pending forensic, pathology reports By Omeiza Ajayi, Abuja The independent ministerial committee investigating the recent deaths of 37 persons in the custody of the Nigerian Security and Civil Defence Corps NSCDC in Minna, Niger State, has asked for two more weeks to submit its report, saying forensic and pathology results were still outstanding. Chairman of the committee, Jonathan Kure, told journalists on Tuesday in Abuja that the panel has already identified troubling lapses as part of its preliminary findings. “There are elements of institutional breakdown. There are elements of overzealousness. Some elements that will require more training for personnel,” he said. The committee which was set up by the Minister of Interior, Hon. Olubunmi Tunji-Ojo, on September 22 was mandated to submit its report within two weeks of its inauguration. It is now seeking an extension from the initial submission date of October 7 to October 21, 2026. Kure said the panel should have handed in its report by now, but the nature of the assignment got in the way. “Because of the timeline given to us, by today we should have turned in our report. But the peculiar nature of this investigation involves a large volume of testimonies and evidence which require our meticulous review and collation,” he said. The committee listed three reasons it could not conclude its work: the large volume of testimony and documentary evidence, the pending forensic and pathology reports “essential to establishing the cause of death”, and “the need to afford all persons implicated, including the officers already suspended, a fair opportunity to respond, so that the Committee’s findings and recommendations will withstand scrutiny and command public confidence.” The committee said “appreciable progress has been recorded”, including inspection of the custody facility, conduct of autopsies, taking of witness statements from NSCDC personnel, survivors, families and other witnesses, and collection of documentary and forensic evidence. Kure said the panel travelled to Minna, where it “was able to have interaction with all the survivors” and met “with bereaved families”. “We were also able to go to the mining site, as well as visiting the State Command Headquarters of the Civil Defence, where we went to the scene of the incident,” he said. According to him, the committee has also met “all the Civil Defence personnel, officers and men that were involved, either directly or indirectly, in that incident. ” He added, “We are still interacting with them. We are not through with that process.” The committee thanked the Ministry of Interior, the NSCDC, the Niger State Government, the Minna Emirate, members of the affected communities and survivors for their cooperation. Assuring Nigerians that the extension would not dilute the work, the chairman said, “We promised Nigerians a thorough job. We are determined to do what is just and what is right, and it will have to be seen to be thorough and credible.” He pledged that “within the next two weeks, we are not going to sleep,” so that the committee can “come back to you, come back to the Minister, and submit a report that will be seen to have done justice where justice is due.” The post Miners’ deaths: Panel finds ‘elements of institutional gaps, overzealousness’ appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.description: El PP mueve ficha el primer día de precampaña y se lanza a la ofensiva contra el PSOE en la Audiencia Nacional. Los populares apenas han tardado 24 horas en solicitar al magistrado Santiago Pedraz, instructor del caso Leire Díez , que impute a la formación de izquierdas como persona jurídica en esas pesquisas por cinco delitos: cohecho, tráfico de influencias, blanqueo, financiación ilegal y malversación. Los conservadores, que encabezan el grupo de acusaciones populares personadas en el sumario, dan este paso después de confiarse a los tribunales para desplegar buena parte de su estrategia de oposición durante esta legislatura. items.title: The 2026 Midterms Must-Watch List
items.description: Subscribe here: Apple Podcasts | Spotify | YouTube | Overcast | Pocket Casts By now, people who have been paying close attention to this year’s midterm elections have a pretty good idea of the state of play: Democrats hope to gain four seats in the Senate and three seats in the House to flip both chambers and have more power to check President Trump’s policy agenda. Republicans, fearing a rout amid the Iran war and its impact on Americans’ lives back home, are hoping to hold on where they can. But the national picture tells only part of the story. When reporters talk about “what voters want,” they are really talking about individuals living lives in different contexts. Every House and Senate race has a unique flavor depending on local problems and which candidate voters believe can help solve them. This week on Radio Atlantic , my colleagues Russell Berman and David Graham join me to zoom in on the races they are paying special attention to as November approaches—for their national implications this time around, and for 2028 and beyond. The following is a transcript of the episode: Russell Berman: The map has become so wide for Democrats, and this is the big surprise of the year right now, as we’re talking in early October. It’s possible that Democrats could lose Michigan and still win the Senate. They have a chance in other red states—Texas, Alaska, even Kansas seems to be very close and competitive right now. Adam Harris: Control over the House and Senate hangs in the balance of this upcoming midterm election. Republicans hope to retain thin majorities in both chambers. But Democrats are hoping to gain four seats in the Senate and three in the House of Representatives, control Congress, and curb President Trump’s power in his final two years. That’s the big picture, but it doesn’t necessarily offer the texture of why Democrats believe they can win back power. The national trends give some indication; Democrats are focusing their message on salient issues: the price of gasoline and household items—often boiled down to the catchall of affordability—and the president’s sinking approval ratings in the shadow of the war in Iran. But national trends can only explain so much. This is Radio Atlantic , I’m Adam Harris, and this week, my colleagues, Atlantic staff writers Russell Berman and David Graham, join me to share the five races they are following most closely this midterm cycle. We’ll discuss why they’re following these contests—beyond the fact that the polls say the races are close—and what they’ll be looking out for in the closing weeks of the campaign. Let’s get to questions. David, Russell, thank you so much for joining me today. Russell Berman: Great to be here. David Graham: My pleasure. Harris: So over the weekend we asked you to think about the five most interesting races to you, and we appreciate your doing so. And today, we’re gonna work through those lists together. We asked you not to share your lists with each other, so everybody’s coming to this fresh. David, I’m going to go to you first. What’s the first race that you want to talk about that you think is important and why? Graham: Let’s talk about the Maine Senate race, which is maybe one that people will be familiar with, but I think one that is just really important and worth talking about. This is where Susan Collins, the longtime Republican incumbent, is running for another term. And she is, after a raucous primary and then withdrawal by Graham Platner, facing off against Troy Jackson, who is another sort of populist Democrat in, I think, an interesting test of both national currents. And also, Maine is a weird state politically, and I think we’re gonna see how that plays out in this race. Harris: Yeah, Russell, I saw you nodding as well. It seems that Maine was on your list too. Berman: Bingo! That was my first one as well. This one should be one—on paper, it should be an easy one, or maybe the easiest, for the Democrats to flip. It is by far the bluest state of the Senate seats where Republicans have an incumbent on the ballot. But as David mentioned, Susan Collins has become a white whale for Democrats over the course of her career. In 2020, she won the state; she beat the polls; she won the state by nine points on the same day that Joe Biden won the state by about the same amount. And that was a huge shocker. And we don’t see as much split-ticket voting as we used to. And so she’s certainly not only one of the more moderate Republican senators, but perhaps the most resilient. And Jackson is more authentically working-class than the last candidate that the Democrats had, Graham Platner. He’s less flawed, as far as we know, but he’s also less charismatic. And so I think that’s one reason why we’re seeing the race go down to the wire, even though the environment is so favorable to Democrats. It was unthinkable that the Democrats could win back the Senate without Maine. And now it’s possible that even if the Democrats win the Senate, as we’ll talk about in other races, they still might have trouble beating Susan Collins. Harris: Why is Susan Collins so strong politically in Maine? Why does she have such staying power? Graham: You have this kind of politician that just sticks around forever, and I think she is one of the few remaining of that type. And to the questions about how Maine is an unusual state—from a national perspective, she does look like a flip-flopper and she has these weird views and she expresses concern about things like Roe v. Wade , but then votes for justices who most people believed correctly would vote to overturn Roe . So she’s in this strange place. But I think maybe that represents some Mainers accurately. And I also think that Maine is a small enough state that she is somebody who people feel like they know. And so she has a credibility with voters that extends past the brand of the Republican Party and extends well before the Trump era as well. Berman: I would add that Democrats in New England in particular—it’s a little bit of a weird thing, which is such a blue area—they like voting for Republicans or moderate Republicans occasionally. So you see this in Vermont, where they’ve elected and reelected a moderate Republican, Phil Scott, as governor, even though they elect and love Bernie Sanders, the most progressive, as of now, senator in the country. And then in Massachusetts, fairly recently, they elected a moderate Republican governor, Charlie Baker, as well. We’re seeing that less in Congress and on the federal level, but Collins is sort of the last of this breed of Republican in New England—or one of the last. And her approval ratings are lower now than they were six years ago, so that’s giving Democrats some hope that this will be different. But Republicans say that the Democrats are basically running the same campaign they’ve run in the past against her and just hoping it’ll work this time. Harris: And does Troy Jackson’s late entry into the race actually change the context of anything? Does it put him in a disadvantage against Collins? Berman: I think it does because Platner was such a lightning rod, obviously, but he had such deep support among people, and it seemed like people who weren’t regular voters and the type of low-propensity voters that Democrats need to get. And Jackson is not as well known—he was a logger before he entered politics up in the northern, more rural part of Maine. He talks like he’s from northern Maine. So that can be compelling but, of course, people have to get to know him, and he hasn’t had as much time. It’s a little bit of the Kamala Harris effect that we might see from two years ago. Harris: So Russell, we’re gonna move out of Maine into your next pick. What’s the next one on your list? Berman: Well, I’ve got one that, Adam, you and I have talked about before—the Michigan Senate race. As we’ve talked about, Democrats need to flip four Republican seats, but that’s only if they hold all of their own seats. And Michigan is the one seat that they currently hold—where the incumbent, Gary Peters, is retiring—that Republicans have a decent chance to flip. And of course, the candidates are Abdul El-Sayed and Mike Rogers. And the big question is whether Abdul El-Sayed, somebody as progressive as he is—he’s another Bernie Sanders type of Democrat. He’s running on Medicare for All. He’s a harsh critic of Israel. He would be the first Muslim elected to the Senate. And can he win in not a blue state like Vermont, but in a purple state like Michigan? And Rogers, of all the Republican candidates—aside from maybe Susan Collins—in the races that we’re watching, is a really strong recruit for Republicans. He is supportive of President Trump, but not super MAGA. He doesn’t have a ton of scandals in his past. He’s a former longtime member of the House with national-security experience, and most importantly, nearly won the state’s other Senate seat just two years ago; he lost narrowly to Elissa Slotkin. And so he’s a middle-of-the-road in this modern era of Republicanism. The polls have El-Sayed up, and I think that’s partially because the national environment is so favorable for Democrats. So this is one that, even though he has a lead, is worth watching until the end. Harris: David, it seemed that Michigan was also on your list. Graham: It was also on my list. And I think it’s interesting—to Russell’s point, I think Mike Rogers is maybe about as close as you can get to a generic Republican in a race. He is a conservative, but he’s not wildly out-there. He is supportive of Trump, but he is not a very clear MAGA candidate. And so you have this almost generic Republican, albeit one with a long reputation in Michigan politics, running against a Democrat who is very much atypical. In his background, he is a medical doctor. He’s atypical in his politics. He’s run for positions before but hasn’t won a statewide race. And so I think it’s a very interesting clash of different styles in that race. Harris: If Democrats lose the seat in Michigan, is there another likely pickup for them? Is there somewhere else that they would be looking if they don’t feel that the seat is as secure? Berman: Well, the map has become so wide for Democrats. And this is the big surprise of the year right now, as we’re talking in early October, is that the answer is yes. Like with Maine, it’s possible that Democrats could lose Michigan and still win the Senate. Now, could they lose Michigan and Maine and win the Senate? Probably not. But they have a chance in other red states—Texas, Alaska, even Kansas seems to be very close and competitive right now. North Carolina is one that they’re probably going to win if the polls are close to right. So it’s possible that they might not need Michigan, but they certainly don’t want to take that risk. Harris: So David, what’s the next one on your list? We’ve got Maine and we’ve got Michigan. Graham: That’s actually a good segue to my next one. I have flagged the Ohio Senate race. And part of this is just home cooking; I grew up in Ohio, so I feel a little bit parochial about this one. But I think this is a really interesting race. We have former Senator Sherrod Brown, a Democrat, running against current Senator Jon Husted, a Republican. Polls have been close. They suggest that maybe Brown is up a little bit in some polls, but it’s fairly close. I think this is interesting. Brown has been such a dominant figure in Ohio politics for a long time. There was a story recently about how voters think of him as the incumbent and don’t really realize that Husted is the incumbent. Berman: That was fascinating; I remember that. Harris: Is it because of the name ID, or? Graham: Yeah. Husted has been in state politics for a long time, but doesn’t have the same sort of name ID and has just been in the Senate for a short time. The last Democrat to win a statewide race in Ohio was one Sherrod Brown. That was in 2018, when he won a Senate seat that he then lost six years later, two years ago. And so to see someone from the Democratic Party win, even one as unusual as Sherrod Brown, I think would be a remarkable moment. I don’t know if it would be a turning point for Ohio politics or just another weird outlier. But I would note that Amy Acton, the Democratic gubernatorial candidate, has also been leading in some polls against former presidential candidate Vivek Ramaswamy, which is not something I would have predicted six, eight, 12 months ago, certainly. Harris: Russell, did you have Ohio? Berman: I didn’t, but only because I was pretty sure David would, given his pedigree in Ohio. But no, it’s a very important race. This part of the country is where Democrats are trying to win back. Iowa is another place where Trump has won after Obama won twice that Democrats might be on the comeback trail. I think the governor’s race, as David mentioned, is fascinating. The other thing for Republicans is that they don’t seem to love any of their candidates, or a lot of their candidates in Ohio. There’s Ramaswamy, and Ramaswamy has other issues in that he can come off kind of arrogant, and he was flying out to the U.S. Open in the middle of the campaign to have a prominent seat there, which wasn’t a good look. And so there’s a question of whether the Republican base, the turnout in Ohio, is worth watching. And so that you might have an interplay up and down the ballot for some of these races. Harris: So what was the third one on your list then? Berman: For me, we have to talk about Texas, right? Is this the year that Texas goes blue? And Democrats, in politics we’ve been watching this for the better part of a decade now, with demographic trends and watching the Hispanic vote, which is obviously huge in Texas. And Democrats have kind of needed a perfect storm, and they might actually have it this year. They have a strong candidate in James Talarico, who’s young and charismatic. They have a ridiculously flawed Republican opponent in Ken Paxton, the attorney general, who had a messy divorce, where his wife is now actually on camera in an ad telling Republicans to vote for the Republican ticket without mentioning the fact that she sued her ex-husband for divorce and he’s the Senate candidate. And then, of course, the Democrats need a strong national environment, and that’s what it looks like they have here. The Hispanic vote is gonna be key. We’re seeing polling out of some House races in southern Texas that looks like the Hispanic vote is swinging back pretty hard toward Democrats after trending toward Republicans in the last couple of elections. And it would just be a huge—to use the cliché—a huge tsunami politically if Democrats did win this Senate seat. We’ve talked about the importance of each of these races for the balance of power, and of course that’s important, but more the symbolic significance of Democrats winning Texas. Then we’d immediately start talking about whether Texas is in play on the presidential level in 2028, which would change the entire political map for both parties. And then, of course, Talarico, if he were to win, would immediately go into the conversation for future national office—because that’s how things work these days—whether it’s in 2028 or later. But Texas is big for a reason, and the Senate seat is fascinating. Harris: David, it seems like Texas was in yours as well. Graham: I did not have the Texas Senate race, partly because I suspected Russell might, but I have a third race that is also in Texas, which is the Fifteenth House District. And Russell is sort of touching on this. This is where Monica De La Cruz, a Republican incumbent, is running for reelection. She won, I believe by 14 points, two years ago; Trump won this direct district by 18 points. And it’s in the Rio Grande Valley, an area that non-Texans got to learn about after the 2024 election as a place where there’s a huge swing from a historically Democratic area toward Republicans and toward Trump, and we were talking a lot about Hispanic shifts in the vote and how enduring this would be. If this race is an indication, it may not be all that enduring. Democrats have a really strong candidate, they believe: a guy named Bobby Pulido, who is a well-known Tejano singer; he has a couple Latin Grammys. He’s a moderate Democrat. I think he’s a really compelling individual, and he seems to be a relatively compelling candidate also. This race looks really close. I think a Pulido win would be a huge moral victory for Democrats and contribute to a potential House majority. I think even if he loses, seeing where the vote comes out in that district will be a really interesting indicator of the Hispanic vote and of the Rio Grande Valley and maybe of the future of Texas as well. Berman: The Democrats actually put out an internal poll—so take it with a grain of salt—that had Pulido winning by 13 points in this race. And this is not, was not seen as like a toss-up race, like one of those dozen or so races that we knew were gonna be close. This is a race that started pretty favorably for Republicans, in part because I’m pretty sure it was made even redder in their gerrymander that they did last year. But of course, when Republicans did all that gerrymandering in Texas, they were basically betting that the Hispanic shift that we saw in the last couple of elections would hold. But if it doesn’t hold, then they could be up the creek, so to speak. This could be a big problem. There’s a couple of other house races in Texas where we could see Democrats win that Republicans kind of thought that they had put in the bag. Harris: When we come back, we work through the rest of David and Russell’s lists. [ Music ] Harris: So David, we have Maine, Michigan, Ohio, Texas House. Russell, so far we have Maine, Michigan, Texas Senate. Russell, what’s your fourth? Berman: My fourth is another red state where Democrats have a decent chance to win for the first time in a while, and that’s all the way out in Alaska. They have a pretty strong centrist type of candidate in Mary Peltola. She has won statewide in Alaska before. She briefly held the at-large House seat there. She lost narrowly in her reelection bid in 2024. And she’s going up against the incumbent, Dan Sullivan, who’s a fairly standard-issue Republican, similar to Mike Rogers in Michigan. But the crazy thing about this race—one of them—is that he’s not the only Dan Sullivan on the ballot. There is another Dan Sullivan who, much to the chagrin of Republicans in Alaska and nationally, was able to get on the ballot. And he could siphon away votes from the senator Dan Sullivan in a close race. The other wrinkle with Alaska is that they use ranked-choice voting. And so it’s possible—we’ve seen ranked-choice voting, as a system, does not advantage either party. But in Alaska, it has seemed to help the more moderate candidate, which tends to be the Democratic candidate, or the other one example there is Lisa Murkowski, who is another moderate survivor among Republicans in the Senate. And so Alaska is one of these states—because the population is so small, it doesn’t take a big shift of voters for it to go the other way. And that’s what Democrats have seen here. On the presidential level, it hasn’t looked completely out of reach. Democrats, some of them joke that they really just need to take, like, 50,000 Democrats from Brooklyn or Washington, D.C., and have them move to Alaska and it could really change the entire equation for them. So this one is interesting. And the Democrats did—unlike in Texas, more recently at least than in Texas—they won a Senate seat in Alaska during a good Democratic year. I believe that was in 2008 with Mark Begich, and he served for a term before losing his reelection bid. So those are the dynamics there. And again, this is one of those races that either could pad—if the Democrats have a really good night—their majority or make their majority. Or it could save their majority if they end up losing in one of these other races that we talked about, like in Maine or Michigan. Harris: All right, we are down to our final race for each of you. David, I’m gonna go to you first. Where are we on the map? Graham: I am once again doing some home cooking, and I’m hoping I can keep Russell on his toes a little bit with this one. I’ve picked out North Carolina’s First District. He saw this coming, probably. Berman: Not exactly, not exactly, but I was like, There’s one of those House races. He’s going against the grain here . ( Laughs .) Graham: So in this race you’ve got Don Davis, who is a moderate Democrat who is running for reelection against Laurie Buckhout, who is a Republican. And he’s running for reelection, but it’s not really in the same district. So this is a race that was—we talked about this a little bit with Texas. This is a map that was redrawn by North Carolina Republicans when President Trump was pushing a lot of Republican legislatures and Republican states to redraw their maps. North Carolina has seen a lot of gerrymandering already, and so there was only so much squeeze left in this map. But they thought they had drawn a map that would be very hard for Don Davis to win. Davis decided to run anyway, which not everyone was sure he would do. And he seems to be running a pretty close race. The polling on this—House polling can be really unreliable; most of the polls are partisan. The Republican polls show Laurie Buckhout up; their Democratic polls show Don Davis up. So it’s hard to know. But I think it’s a really interesting test of this Republican gerrymandering and whether we might be pushing into what they call dummy-mander territory, where you just stretch your voters out so much that you end up not being able to win these districts. I was out in this district a couple months ago, and there were billboards up that said Don Davis, he’s one of us . Not Don Davis, he’s a Democrat , notably. And so I’ll be curious to see also, regardless of who wins this race, where it comes down and what that tells us about the gerrymandering push that we saw around the country. Harris: And Russell, what’s your big five? Berman: Well, we’re staying in the same region and we’re going down to South Carolina. And that’s the First District there. This is in and around Charleston; the Low Country, around Charleston, includes Hilton Head. And so this is the race that is the seat that is currently held by Nancy Mace. She is a social-media star, if you will, but she is not very popular anymore in her district. And she’s not running for reelection—she ran for governor and she lost pretty badly. And the fact that she’s unpopular in her district is one of the factors that’s helping Democrats. And the Democrats have a very interesting candidate in Nancy—another Nancy—a Nancy Lacore, who is a former Republican and she was the chief of the Navy Reserve until Pete Hegseth fired her last year. She was among many military leaders that he fired and continues to fire; many of them are women or people of color. And this is a seat that’s not a toss-up. This is one where if the Democratic wave is pretty big, it’s going to continue—again the metaphor and the cliché—to wash over places like South Carolina’s First District. Because this is a district that does still lean Republican. Democrats actually won the seat in their last wave year, in the Trump midterm in 2018. A moderate named Joe Cunningham, in pretty big surprise, won this seat, and then he lost two years later to Nancy Mace. And then the Republicans gerrymandered the seat to make it a little bit more Republican and help them hold it. And so that’s making it still a pretty tough seat for Democrats to win. But the Democrats—as David mentioned, these polls are partisan, but they have a poll showing that it’s very close. They seem cautiously optimistic, in part because of Mace’s unpopularity there. The Republican candidate is a woman named Jenny Costa Honeycutt, who seems to be a perfectly fine candidate, but it’s telling that she’s running a campaign where she is running against what she calls clickbait politics, which seems to be a not-so-veiled reference to, I am not Nancy Mace; I will be a different type of member of Congress . So this is one that I’m actually heading down to report on and I’ll be watching closely. Harris: We’ve zoomed in a lot, y’all. I wanna broaden us back out to bring it to a close. If you had to draw a through line out from your list heading into the midterms, what is the through line to your list? Berman: Well, it’s not on all of them, but on a lot of them it’s Democrats trying to make inroads in red areas in a way that can really unlock a lot of new territory for them in future elections. If they’re able to make these connections with voters, if they actually win these races and then govern in a way that the voters like, it could change the political map going forward in a way that we haven’t seen on the Democratic side since really the Obama era in their first midterm win, during the Bush years in 2006 and 2008, with Obama. And so I think that is a through line. And then of course, the obvious one is just how unpopular President Trump is and the impact that’s having on Republican candidates in, again, these states that they usually win pretty easily. Harris: And David, for yours? Graham: One other thing that I note going through my list, through most of these races, is just these candidates who have particular connections or routes to electorates. You look at a guy like Bobby Pulido, you look at a guy like Sherrod Brown, who seems to be the only Democrat, maybe, who can win a statewide in Ohio. You look at Don Davis, somebody who’s saying he’s one of us. You look at Troy Jackson, who’s a logger, but also Susan Collins, who’s had that race for a long time. And so, although there are big national waves and big national currents, and I think the economy and Trump’s unpopularity are so dominant, what does make a lot of difference in these races are the way voters connect with individual candidates and the way candidates can connect with the voters. Harris: Well, David, Russell, thank you so much for helping us process the big national picture and understand it at a more local, granular level as we head towards the midterm elections. You’ve given a lot for us to think about. And thank you so much for joining me this morning. Berman: It was great, thanks. Graham: Thank you.

items.title: Vers une résurgence du mouvement des Gilets jaunes ?
items.description: Depuis la fin de l'été, les données du moteur de recherche Google montrent un pic d'intérêt en France pour les Gilets jaunes : l'indice de recherche, qui stagnait sous 10 depuis le début de l'année, a bondi autour de 60, son plus haut niveau depuis janvier 2023. D'autres termes associés, comme « Gilets jaunes 2026 », ont atteint des niveaux record. Sur les réseaux sociaux, les appels à l’organisation de nouveaux rassemblements le 17 octobre se multiplient. Le mouvement des Gilets jaunes, principalement actif à l’hiver 2018-2019, a connu quelques résurgences ces dernières années, notamment en 2023, dans le cadre du mouvement contre la réforme des retraites. Son hétérogénéité et sa décentralisation le rendent toutefois largement imprévisible, et il est difficile d'anticiper une éventuelle reprise du blocage des ronds-points, lancé fin 2018 en partie en réaction à la hausse des taxes sur les carburants. Une potentielle convergence avec le mouvement lancé par les lycéens et les étudiants le 1er octobre pourrait donner lieu à des manifestations d’ampleur, bien qu’aucun syndicat majeur ne semble pour l’heure s’être joint à la date du 17 octobre. Des figures historiques du mouvement des Gilest jaunes, comme le militant Jérôme Rodrigues, affirment par ailleurs ne pas savoir d’où proviennent ces appels au rassemblement, qui reposent notamment sur des images de manifestants portant des Gilets jaunes générées par l’intelligence artificielle Appel à manifester le 17 octobre : y a-t-il une réalité derrière cette tendance des réseaux sociaux ? », Public Sénat , 18 septembre 2026.'> 1 . Le contexte de hausse du prix de l’essence et de baisse du pouvoir d’achat évoque celui de 2018, lorsque le prix du sans plomb 95 avait augmenté de plus de 5 % sur la période janvier-août, et dépassait 1,5 euro le litre en septembre. Cette année, alors que le conflit se poursuit au Moyen-Orient, le prix à la pompe du sans plomb 95 a enregistré une hausse de près de 20 % sur cette même période, passant de 1,72 euro le litre en janvier à 2,05 euros en août, selon les chiffres de l’Insee. Dans certaines stations-essence, le prix du SP-95 est supérieur à 2,5 euros au mardi 6 octobre, avec des pics frôlant les 3 euros. Près d’un quart des lycées du pays (891 sur environ 3 700) ont vu des cours être suspendus ou annulés en raison du mouvement de blocage. En prenant en compte les prévisions policières et les chiffres du ministère de l’Intérieur et de la CGT, entre 100 000 et 300 000 personnes auraient manifesté mardi 6 octobre au matin. La première journée d'action des Gilets jaunes, le 17 novembre 2018, avait rassemblé, au plus fort, jusqu’à 290 000 personnes selon Beauvau, et jusqu'à 1,3 million selon le syndicat France Police – Policiers en colère. Le mouvement contre la réforme des retraites, au premier semestre 2023, reste la plus forte mobilisation sociale de ces dernières années : le 7 mars, la CGT avait dénombré 3,5 millions de manifestants, contre 1,3 million pour le ministère de l'Intérieur. L’article Vers une résurgence du mouvement des Gilets jaunes ? est apparu en premier sur Le Grand Continent .

items.title: Deux décés et un blessé au Parcelles assainies: émoi et consternation à l’Unité 7
items.description: Les pluies diluviennes enregistrées dimanche 4 octobre à l’unité 7 des Parcelles Assainies ont fait deux victimes : A. Sène et son fils Mb. Gningue. Dans ce quartier, les populations réclament un système d’évacuation des eaux ainsi que le pavage des rues. Lundi 5 octobre 2026. 12 heures passées. Le soleil projette ses rayons sur Dakar, au lendemain des fortes pluies et des inondations. Aux Parcelles Assainies, c’est une journée de tristesse, d’émoi et de consternation. L’unité 7 reste l’un des endroits les plus touchés. Sur place, hommes, femmes et jeunes se déploient pour pomper les eaux qui envahissent les lieux. Des habits mouillés, des bagages engloutis, des gousses d’ail et autres condiments flottent à la surface, tandis que des détritus de toutes sortes jonchent les lieux. Devant la maison mortuaire, dont le mur de clôture a été endommagé par les fortes pluies, une chaîne humaine s’est formée. Les jeunes, munis de seaux, s’activent pour évacuer les eaux. Selon le commissaire Sow des Parcelles Assainies, que nous avons joint au téléphone, c’est dimanche 4 octobre, vers 18 h 30, qu’il a été informé de la mort de deux personnes : A. Sène, âgée de 25 ans, et son fils Mb. Gningue, âgé de 3 à 4 ans. D’après Soulèye Serigne Thiané, gestionnaire de la salle du foyer socio-culturel Demba Dia, un blessé, Pape Alassane Faye, a également été enregistré. Celui-ci a subi un traumatisme au genou droit, à la cheville du même pied ainsi que quelques égratignures. Il est d’ailleurs pris en charge par la mairie des Parcelles Assainies. À en croire Fallou Sarr, gérant de cette maison où vivaient 36 personnes, les pluies du dimanche 4 octobre ont causé d’importants dégâts. « L’eau est venue avec une très grande vitesse ; elle débordait de partout. Nous étions en train de charger des sacs de sable pour l’arrêter, tandis que d’autres essayaient de tracer des sillons pour l’évacuer. C’est à ce moment qu’elle a fait tomber un pan important du mur de clôture pour entrer dans la maison », explique-t-il. Les deux victimes, qui dormaient, ont été surprises par les eaux. Nuit blanche Dépassés par les événements, les colocataires se sont réfugiés au premier étage, tandis que les deux victimes manquaient à l’appel. « Depuis 48 heures, nous dormons à la belle étoile ; d’autres sont hébergés à la mairie des Parcelles Assainies. Nos habits ne sont pas changés. Nous n’avons ni mangé ni bu, mais nous rendons grâce à Dieu », témoigne, en pleurs, Fallou Sarr. Pour Ousmane Sarr, qui habite l’unité 7, les habitants de la cité Senelec vivent un véritable calvaire à chaque épisode pluvieux depuis plus de 20 ans. « Je mesure près de 1,95 m. Mon petit frère est plus grand que moi, mais lorsqu’il est entré dans la maison, il a failli se noyer. Il est immédiatement ressorti. Ce sont des jeunes du quartier qui ont pris une échelle pour passer dans la maison mitoyenne et faire remonter les deux victimes, qui étaient déjà sans vie », raconte-t-il. Poursuivant, il dénonce l’absence de système d’évacuation des eaux et de curage des canaux, l’ensablement qui crée des pentes ou des descentes par endroits, ainsi que certains charretiers qui déverseraient des gravats dans le quartier. « Il nous faut un pavage des rues », sollicite-t-il. La même demande est formulée par Oustaz Baye Thiam, de l’école franco-arabe El Hadji Omar Ngoné. Le locataire de la maison endeuillée, Youssoupha Ba, révèle : « J’habite les lieux depuis deux ans, mais c’est la première fois que j’assiste à un tel scénario. Nous avons tout perdu : habits, téléphones, matelas, couvertures ». Même son de cloche chez son colocataire, Ibrahima Diongue, ouvrier dans une usine de biscuits. Le regard hagard, il dit avoir perdu de l’argent. À l’école franco-arabe Mame Diarra Bousso de l’unité 7 des Parcelles Assainies, l’enceinte de l’établissement est également engloutie par les eaux. Un pan du mur s’est effondré. Khadim Ndiaye, élève en classe de seconde au lycée des Parcelles Assainies, explique : « Nous avons tenté d’évacuer l’eau jusqu’à 2 heures du matin. Le lendemain, nous sommes revenus à la charge à 9 heures. Les pluies ont causé de graves dégâts matériels. Le système de pompage de l’Onas ne fonctionne pas bien ; durant la pluie, l’eau s’est mélangée aux eaux des fosses septiques ». Sadikh Sène, agent à l’Office national de l’assainissement du Sénégal (Onas), confirme que ses appareils électroménagers, matelas, habits et chaussures ont été mouillés par les eaux. « Le dispositif pompait normalement, mais il a beaucoup plu avant-hier. Les deux stations n’assurent pas le même rôle : l’une est réservée aux eaux pluviales, l’autre aux eaux usées », précise-t-il. Au foyer socio-éducatif Demba Dia, 15 sinistrés de nationalités différentes sont hébergés. L’ensemble des biens perdus a été inventorié. Dans l’après-midi, le ministre de l’Intérieur, Mouhamadou Makhtar Cissé, et le ministre de l’Hydraulique et de l’Assainissement, Dr Cheikh Tidiane Dièye, se sont rendus aux Parcelles Assainies pour apporter le message de compassion et de soutien du chef de l’État, Bassirou Diomaye Faye. Par Serigne Mansour Sy CISSÉ

items.title: PAC steps down 2 special audit reports into Ghana’s US Embassy, 13th All African Games
items.description: Parliament’s Public Accounts Committee (PAC) has stepped down two special audit reports covering Ghana’s Embassy in Washington, DC, and the 13th All African Games after the Auditor-General withdrew the reports. The Committee announced the development as it began examining the Auditor-General’s reports on financial irregularities recorded in 2025. The special audit report on Ghana’s Embassy in Washington, DC, covered the period from 2017 to 2025. According to the Public Accounts Committee, the report will not be considered during the current sittings because the Auditor-General has formally written to Parliament to withdraw it. The Committee also said the special audit report on the 13th All African Games has been dropped and will not be examined at this stage. Ms Osei Asare, speaking on the matter, said the decision followed a debriefing between the Committee and the Auditor-General. “The special audit report on the Embassy of Ghana in Washington, DC, covering 2017 to 2025 will not be considered in these sittings.” He explained that the Auditor-General communicated the withdrawal of the Embassy report to Parliament through a formal letter. “Through a letter by the Auditor-General to Parliament has written to withdraw this particular report.” On the 13th All African Games report, she said the Committee reached a similar decision following discussions with the Auditor-General. “Again, the report on the 13th All African Games was also stepped down during our debriefing with the Auditor-General.” She stressed that the withdrawal does not mean the matters contained in the reports have been permanently abandoned, indicating that the Committee will consider them when the reports are brought back. “We will not be looking at these two reports until they are brought back to us again.” The Public Accounts Committee said it was important for the public to be informed about the decision, given the Committee’s responsibility to examine findings contained in the Auditor-General’s reports. The announcement comes as the Committee begins a broader examination of financial irregularities recorded in the 2025 audit reports. While the two special audits have been removed from the current agenda, the Committee is turning its attention to the Auditor-General’s Ministries, Departments and Agencies Audit Report for 2025. The report has identified financial irregularities amounting to GH¢5.2 billion. The Committee says one of its major concerns is the scale of tax-related infractions contained in the report. According to the Committee, approximately GH¢4.8 billion of the reported irregularities relate to tax infractions. The Committee says it will seek answers on the nature of the tax breaches and determine what steps the relevant tax authorities have taken to address them. “We see a reported financial irregularity of five point two billion. But the most alarming thing is the tax infraction of four point eight billion.” The Committee intends to establish whether the affected institutions have taken corrective measures and whether the amounts involved have been recovered or otherwise addressed. The Committee has also announced a change in the way it intends to examine audit findings. Rather than simply asking institutions to respond to individual infractions, the Committee says it will focus more heavily on whether public institutions have acted on previous audit recommendations. The move follows concerns that some institutions continue to appear in audit reports for similar control failures year after year. The Committee says repeated findings may indicate that institutions are not implementing recommendations or correcting weaknesses identified by the Auditor-General. “A legitimate concern of the Ghanaian public is that many audit findings appear year after year.” The Committee says that where the same institution is repeatedly cited for the same control failure, the issue goes beyond the existence of an audit finding. According to the Committee, institutions appearing before it will be expected to demonstrate what corrective action has been taken and how those measures have prevented the recurrence of financial irregularities. The new approach is intended to make the parliamentary scrutiny of audit reports more focused on results and accountability rather than simply recording infractions. For now, however, the special audit reports on Ghana’s Embassy in Washington, DC, and the 13th All African Games remain outside the Committee’s current proceedings following their withdrawal and subsequent stepping down. The Committee says it will revisit both reports when they are formally brought back before it.

items.title: Missing Lao Critic in Thailand Feared ‘Disappeared’
items.description: Click to expand Image Flags of member countries fly at the ASEAN Secretariat in Jakarta, Indonesia, April 22, 2021. © 2021 AP Photo/Tatan Syuflana, File Three weeks ago, 26-year-old Lao activist Khieo Lapchanh, an asylum seeker in Thailand, vanished in Samut Sakhon province following his shift at the restaurant where he worked. Khieo’s disappearance in the early hours of September 15 came one day before his first interview with the United Nations refugee agency (UNHCR) in Bangkok. Thai authorities have yet to provide any information regarding his whereabouts. Khieo had been posting videos critical of the Lao government to his Facebook page, Khiew Channel, which had about 158,000 followers. According to Manushya Foundation, a rights group that supported him, he had faced coordinated harassment, doxxing, and death threats. After Lao officials visited his mother's home in Laos this year on March 31 and April 17 concerning his activities, Khieo stopped posting political content. Given the threats he faced and the history of enforced disappearances of Lao activists both in Laos and abroad, Thai authorities should urgently locate him. On September 27, Human Rights Watch visited the area near the restaurant where Khieo worked and the building where he lived. Several businesses with cameras facing the street said their footage from the night of September 15 had already been automatically deleted. Khieo's case fits a troubling pattern of Lao activists abroad being targeted by transnational repression: efforts by governments or their agents to silence dissent by committing human rights abuses against their nationals or diaspora members outside their territorial jurisdiction. Od Sayavong, a Lao democracy activist and UNHCR-recognized refugee, forcibly disappeared in Bangkok in August 2019. His fate remains unknown and the Thai police investigation stalled. In May 2023, Lao activist Bounsuan Kitiyano was shot dead in Thailand’s Ubon Ratchathani province. Thailand has committed to preventing enforced disappearances under domestic and international law. The Prevention and Suppression of Torture and Enforced Disappearance Act, in force since February 2023, obligates Thai authorities to investigate cases in which state involvement is possible, and allows the Department of Special Investigation to take over such cases. Thai authorities have not said whether they are treating Khieo's case under this law. They should immediately escalate the investigation and make genuine efforts to find out what happened to Khieo. Concerned governments should also press Lao authorities for any information about Khieo Lapchanh's whereabouts, including whether he is in their custody.

items.title: PM Shehbaz orders gas load management plan for winter, steps for ensuring uninterrupted imports
items.description: Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif on Tuesday directed the relevant authorities to prepare a comprehensive plan for gas load management and take all necessary measures to ensure uninterrupted gas imports during the winter season, given the regional situation. He issued these instructions while chairing a meeting on gas load management during the winter season, held in Islamabad, a statement by the Prime Minister’s Office (PMO) said. “The prime minister directed that a comprehensive plan be devised for gas load management, all necessary measures be taken in advance, an extensive public awareness campaign on the implementation of the gas load management plan be launched and all necessary steps be taken to ensure uninterrupted gas imports, keeping in view the current regional situation,” the PMO said. The meeting was also briefed on measures taken in advance for gas load management, the statement added. The participants were informed that domestic consumers would be given priority for the supply of locally produced gas while RLNG would be prioritised for power generation and industries, it said. Moreover, a public awareness campaign would be launched to promote alternative energy sources at the household level in place of locally supplied gas, according to the statement. “Measures are also being taken to ensure the uninterrupted transmission of gas from reserves in the northern regions of the country,” the PMO said, adding that a proposal to introduce bank financing facilities for electric appliances used for water and space heating was also under consideration. The meeting was attended by National Food Security Minister Rana Tanveer Hussain, Economic Affairs Minister Ahad Khan Cheema, Finance Minister Muhammad Aurangzeb, Petroleum Minister Ali Pervaiz Malik, Adviser to the Prime Minister on Industry Haroon Akhtar, Minister of State for Finance and Railways Bilal Azhar Kayani and relevant senior government officials. The meeting took place as the authorities struggle to finalise the liquefied natural gas (LNG) import plan for the upcoming three winter months — December to February — amid a challenging supply situation stemming from the US-Iran conflict. Renewed hostilities in the Middle East have resulted in disruption of major oil and gas supply routes — the Strait of Hormuz and Bab al-Mandab — and caused fuel prices to rise. Against this backdrop, gas companies and the Petroleum Division had sought at least 22 import cargoes for the three-month period, but the task force on energy, led by Lt Gen Zafar Iqbal, has promised no more than 10-12 cargoes of around 100 million cubic feet each on a best-effort basis, using all diplomatic and logistical channels. The plan will be presented to the prime minister for approval, given the involvement of around $100m per spot cargo and the requirement for consent from the Ministry of Finance and the State Bank of Pakistan. The matter has assumed greater importance because the LNG import plan will affect the current account targets agreed upon by the Ministry of Finance and the International Monetary Fund, whose staff mission is c urrently in Pakistan and holding talks that could pave the way for the disbursement of about $1.2 billion under two concurrent programmes. Sources, meanwhile, indicate that actual LNG imports may not exceed seven to eight cargoes over the three winter months, given prevailing market conditions, which would bring the outcome closer to the Ministry of Finance’s desired level. In a related development, the Oil and Gas Regulatory Authority (Ogra) has notified an eight per cent increase in liquefied petroleum gas (LPG), raising the cost of the 11.8kg domestic cylinder by Rs244.14 for October.

items.title: Kloto : Une campagne pour zéro grossesse en milieu scolaire lancée au lycée de Kpodzi
items.description: Kpalimé, 6 oct. (ATOP) – Le directeur régional de l’Éducation des Plateaux-Ouest, Sanla Mintchiébe, a donné, le lundi 5 octobre au lycée de Kpodzi, le coup d’envoi de la campagne de sensibilisation contre les grossesses en milieu scolaire dans les écoles. Initiée par la Croix-Rouge togolaise en collaboration avec la direction préfectorale de la Santé (DPS) de Kloto et le ministère de l’Éducation nationale, cette campagne vise à renforcer la prévention auprès des apprenants et à parvenir à zéro grossesse dans les établissements scolaires de la région éducative des Plateaux-Ouest. Elle entend informer les apprenants sur les risques, les dangers et les conséquences des grossesses précoces. Pour cette troisième édition, la Croix-Rouge a introduit une innovation avec l’organisation d’un concours de sketch inter établissement afin de permettre aux élèves eux-mêmes de porter les messages de sensibilisation auprès de leurs camarades à travers le sketch, l’humour et la créativité. Les sketchs aborderont les risques liés aux grossesses précoces, le harcèlement, la pression des pairs et l’importance de savoir résister à la pression. Les établissements ciblés sont les CEG et les lycées de Kloto 1. Les animatrices, le club de la croix rouge du lycée et le DRE Mme Bintou Kassim Nayao, sage-femme, responsable de la santé de la reproduction et Mme Pikli Bidenam, sage-femme, responsable de la santé des jeunes et adolescents à la DPS Kloto ont entretenu les élèves sur les causes, les conséquences et les moyens de prévention des grossesses précoces. Elles ont énuméré les facteurs favorisant le phénomène, notamment la recherche de gains faciles, du plaisir sexuel, l’irresponsabilité de certains parents et les mauvaises fréquentations. Les conséquences, selon elles, sont l’abandon des études, le rejet familial et les risques liés aux avortements clandestins. Pour éviter ces grossesses précoces en milieux scolaires, les deux oratrices ont conseillé les élèves de privilégier l’abstinence, d’éviter les mauvaises fréquentations et les rapports sexuels non protégés, de se concentrer sur leurs études et de suivre les conseils des parents et des enseignants. Elles ont invité les apprenants à éviter l’exposition aux contenus pornographiques susceptibles, selon elles, d’influencer négativement leurs comportements. Le directeur régional de l’Éducation des Plateaux-Ouest a souligné que les grossesses en milieu scolaire constituent une « perte nationale », aussi bien pour les apprenants et leurs familles que pour l’État. Il a appelé les élèves à se fixer des objectifs et à faire de la réussite scolaire leur priorité. Le président de la croix rouge, section locale de Kpalimé, Stan Kokou Awanou a exhorté les apprenants à rester concentrés sur leurs études et à éviter les comportements susceptibles de compromettre leur avenir. Il a invité les parents, les chefs d’établissements et les autorités à accompagner cette initiative de la croix rouge. La campagne de sensibilisation se poursuit dans les établissements scolaires de la région éducative des Plateaux-Ouest, avec pour ambition d’atteindre l’objectif de zéro grossesse en milieu scolaire au cours de l’année scolaire 2026-2027. ATOP/AYH/HKM

items.title: Drama in Anambra court as pastor’s supporters attack journalists
items.description: By Vincent Ujumadu AWKA — There was a mild drama at the Anambra State High Court, Awka, on Tuesday as persons suspected to be supporters and church members of the General Overseer of Dayspring Assembly, Awada-Obosi, Pastor Harrison Anazodo, allegedly attacked journalists and cameramen while attempting to shield him from the media. The incident occurred as Anazodo arrived at the court for his trial before Justice Jude Obiora. The pastor was arrested by officials of the Anambra State Government on June 10, 2026, and is facing a seven-count charge bordering on alleged propagation of the accumulation of wealth through supernatural means, an offence proscribed under the Anambra State Homeland Security Law 2025, as well as alleged murder. He is also accused of abduction, unlawful separation and isolation of individuals from their families and keeping them at his residence. Eyewitnesses said some of the pastor’s supporters used umbrellas and their hands to shield him from cameras, while allegedly pushing journalists away from the vehicle that conveyed him to the court. Two or three journalists reportedly had their mobile phones damaged during the altercation. The supporters also reportedly occupied virtually every available space in the courtroom, leaving little room for other persons seeking to observe the proceedings. Speaking with journalists after the proceedings, the state Attorney-General and Commissioner for Justice, Barr. Tobechukwu Nweke, SAN, condemned the incident. Nweke said: “My attention was drawn to the fact that the defendant standing criminal trial, Pastor Harrison Anazodo, came to the court premises with some persons who attacked journalists and damaged their gadgets. “I had to enter the courtroom and inform the court of the unfortunate incident, for two reasons: first, the court premises and the courtroom are hallowed places, and secondly, journalists are the eyes and ears of the public and must be respected at all times.” He said he condemned the conduct, brought it to the attention of the court and requested that it be recorded in the proceedings. “I indicated that I would escalate it to law enforcement authorities,” Nweke added. According to the Attorney-General, counsel to the defendant subsequently apologised to him, members of the press and the court and accepted responsibility for replacing the damaged gadgets. “The court delivered a bench ruling accepting the apology, directed that the gadgets be replaced, and appealed to me to let the matter rest. This is fundamental to the extent that it reemphasizes the freedom of the press to carry out their duties,” he said. Nweke added that the court further ordered that proceedings in the matter would remain public and accessible to the press, stressing that no journalist should be harassed during subsequent hearings. He warned that any recurrence of such conduct could lead to the trial being conducted on camera. The post Drama in Anambra court as pastor’s supporters attack journalists appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Yellow Fever outbreak kills 7 in Sissala East
items.description: At least seven people have died following a confirmed Yellow Fever outbreak in the Sissala East Municipality of the Upper West Region, with children and young people reportedly among the worst affected. The Municipal Health Directorate has confirmed the outbreak, with several cases concentrated in the municipality. Residents say most of those affected are children and young people between the ages of zero and 25, raising concerns over the spread and severity of the disease. The situation has sparked anxiety among residents, particularly in communities where the deaths have been recorded. The Fulani chief in one of the worst-affected communities described the situation as extremely disturbing, saying several children have died under circumstances that initially raised concerns about a possible new disease. According to him, the first reported case involved a child who was taken to the hospital and subsequently referred for further treatment but died two days later. “Children are indeed dying here. The first case was reported at the hospital, and the child was referred to the hospital, but he unfortunately died two days later, blood coming out of his nostrils and mouth,” he said. The chief said his concerns intensified as the number of deaths increased. He explained that after four deaths had been recorded, he contacted health officials and urged them to investigate the circumstances surrounding the deaths. “When the number of deaths got to four, I told them it may be a new disease. They promised to check it and report it to their superiors.” However, according to the chief, more children continued to die after the initial concerns were raised, compelling him to escalate the matter to the Tumu Traditional Council.

items.description: Kpalimé, 6 oct. (ATOP) – La 4 ème session ordinaire de l’année 2026 des communes Kloto 1 et 3, consacrées à la préparation des budgets primitifs exercice 2027 et la définition des priorités de développement ont été ouvertes le lundi 5 octobre respectivement à Kpalimé et à Kuma-Konda. Les cérémonies ont été présidées par le préfet de Kloto, Koku Bertin Assan en présence de la sénatrice, des députés et des chefs traditionnels de la préfecture. Les travaux des deux sessions doivent aboutir à des décisions et orientations destinées à renforcer la mobilisation des ressources et à améliorer les conditions de vie des populations. Conseillers, officiels et invités dans la commune de Kloto 3 Dans la commune Kloto 1, le maire Apelete Kossi Atigaku a appelé les conseillers municipaux à tirer les enseignements de l’exécution budgétaire en cours et à intégrer les besoins prioritaires de la population. Il a notamment cité l’amélioration du cadre de vie, la gestion des déchets, la salubrité, la lutte contre la divagation des animaux, la modernisation de l’administration communale et le renforcement de la participation citoyenne. Le maire a également insisté sur la nécessité de diversifier les sources de recettes de la commune afin de mieux financer son développement. Le préfet a encouragé les conseillers à poursuivre l’amélioration de la mobilisation des recettes et à privilégier une démarche participative dans l’élaboration du budget. Il a également appelé à renforcer la salubrité, à libérer les abords des routes et à faire respecter les règles relatives à l’occupation des espaces publics pour améliorer l’attractivité de Kpalimé. Dans la commune Kloto 3, les conseillers vont aussi examiner le rapport de la situation financière, le bilan des réalisations entreprises dans la commune. Ils feront également des débats sur l’orientation budgétaire. Le maire Yawo Asagbé a invité les différents acteurs à privilégier le dialogue et l’intérêt général. M. Assan a exhorté le conseil municipal à élaborer un budget participatif, fondé sur les réalités et potentialités de la commune. Il a également demandé aux élus locaux de rechercher de nouvelles sources de financement, à travers la fiscalité et la valorisation du tourisme, tout en insistant sur la salubrité et la transparence dans la gestion communale. items.title: UN chief hails Pakistan's 'pivotal role' in US-Iran conflict, calls for 'return to diplomacy'
items.description: United Nations Secretary General Antonio Guterres on Tuesday lauded Pakistan’s “pivotal role” in mediating between the United States and Iran as he called on the parties to end the conflict and return to diplomacy. Addressing a press conference in Islamabad alongside Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Ishaq Dar, he said: “Pakistan’s spirit of engagement is front and centre on issues of international peace and security. “I salute Pakistan’s leadership for helping to create the conditions for dialogue between the US and Iran and mediating that conflict. Your efforts helped deliver the Islamabad memorandum of understanding , the subsequent ceasefire and the framework for future negotiations . Every Pakistani should be proud of that pivotal role,” he said. “And from Islamabad, I want to send a loud and clear message to all parties: end the conflict, return to diplomacy and restore navigational rights in accordance with international law. There will never be peace in the region until the right of self-determination of the Palestinian people is recognised, as Pakistan has long championed,” he said. At the outset of his speech, the UN chief said that it was “wonderful to be back in Pakistan”. “I am in the closing months of my tenure as UN secretary general. Before that, I served ten years as UN high commissioner for refugees,” he said. “Pakistan has shown that, even in difficult circumstances, perhaps especially in difficult circumstances, compassion and responsibility must go hand-in-hand,” he said. He asserted that Pakistan mattered not only because of its size, but because it brought an “essential perspective” to global debates. “For decades, Pakistan opened its doors to millions of Afghans fleeing conflict and instability. Communities around this country shared whatever they had with people seeking protection and safety,” Guterres said. He added that the UN was committed to working together with the country to uphold protection principles and ensure that returns of Afghans “proceed in a voluntary, safe and dignified way”. According to the UN chief, Pakistan had put a spotlight on the value of multilateralism, dialogue, mediation and diplomacy at a time of growing division and mistrust around the world. “Those same values are vital within societies as well,” he stated. “Here and around the world, we know that inclusive institutions, respect for human rights, and a vibrant civic space are necessary to help strengthen social cohesion, build trust and enable people to contribute fully to their country’s future.” Guterres also appreciated Pakistan’s contributions to United Nations peacekeeping. “Pakistani women and men have served with courage and distinction in some of the most difficult and dangerous environments,” he said. “More than 180 brave Pakistani souls gave their lives in the service of peace. We honour their sacrifice.” The chief highlighted Pakistan’s leadership with Denmark on UN Security Council (UNSC) resolution 2823, which strengthened accountability for crimes against UN peacekeepers. One hundred and fifty-three countries co-sponsored the resolution, which according to Guterres, was the largest number of co-sponsors for a UNSC resolution in UN history. The UN chief also shared his plans to visit United Nations Military Observer Group in India and Pakistan (UNMOGIP) later in the day to pay tribute to the mission and to peacekeepers worldwide. Commenting on terrorism in the country, he said: “Pakistan has endured immense suffering. Thousands of people lost their lives. Families and communities across the country continue to bear scars. We stand with Pakistan in confronting this threat of terrorism.” He added that addressing terrorism and legitimate security concerns was necessary and indispensable. “Experience shows that the strongest and most effective security responses are those grounded in international law, human rights and the rule of law.” Towards the end of his speech, Guterres spoke about the climate crisis. “My last visit to Pakistan came during the catastrophic floods of 2022. I will never forget the utter devastation I saw,” he said, referring to the unprecedented floods four years ago that affected approximately 33 million people and claimed the lives of 1,700 people. “But I also saw the resilience, determination and solidarity of the Pakistani people,” Guterres said. “Pakistan is on the frontlines of climate chaos despite contributing only a tiny fraction of global emissions.” He appreciated Pakistan’s response to the crises, including establishment of the Loss and Damage Fund and the country’s growing clean energy transition. However, he asserted that leadership from vulnerable developing countries cannot substitute for responsibility from developed countries. “The G20 represents 80 per cent of global emissions. We need a drastic reduction in those emissions this decade,” he highlighted. “The principle of common but differentiated responsibilities must apply, but all countries must do their part,” he said. Meanwhile, Dar said he “greatly appreciated” Guterres’ visit, which he asserted was a reflection of the “long-standing and close cooperation” between Pakistan and the UN. “It also shows our common resolve to strengthen multilateralism and our cooperation at a time of profound global challenges,” he said. “We have consistently sought to uphold the purposes and principles of the UN charter, advance international peace and security, contribute to peacekeeping and strengthen multilateral solutions to global challenges.” Dar referred to Guterres as a “great friend” of Pakistan, adding that the country would not forget his solidarity during the 2022 floods as well as his efforts to mobilise international support for recovery and reconstruction. During its time as an elected member of the UNSC, Dar said Pakistan had tried to make “significant contributions” to international peace and security, with particular emphasis on dialogue, diplomacy, and the peaceful settlement of disputes. “Our initiative on resolution 2788 on strengthening multilateralism and mechanisms for the peaceful settlement of disputes is a reflection of Pakistan’s approach in this regard,” the minister recalled. “The unanimous adoption of that resolution reaffirmed the importance of negotiation, mediation, preventive diplomacy, and the good offices of the UN secretary general.” He appreciated Guterres’ engagement with the follow-up to the resolution, including the participation and presentation of “solid recommendations” in the open debate held in July this year. Dar said the country valued the secretary general’s “readiness” to extend his good offices in situations where dialogue and diplomacy could help reduce tensions and create space for peaceful solutions. “This is particularly relevant at a time when the international community is confronted with multiple conflicts and crises,” he reiterated. “Pakistan believes that the UN must remain at the centre of international efforts to address these challenges and that diplomacy must be given every opportunity to succeed.” Pakistan, Dar said, had played a “proactive and constructive” role in promoting dialogue and de-escalation in the Gulf region. He appreciated Guterres’ support for Pakistan’s mediation efforts and his recognition of the importance of diplomatic engagement. “Pakistan’s role in facilitating dialogue is consistent with our broader approach at the UN, which is to promote cooperation over confrontation, dialogue over conflict and peaceful settlement over the use of force,” he stated. The minister said Pakistan supported the chief’s UN80 initiative, which seeks to make the UN more “effective, efficient and fit for purpose”. “We believe that efforts to strengthen the organisation must reinforce its ability to deliver on its core mandates, while ensuring that the priorities and concerns of developing countries remain central.” According to him, stronger, effective, inclusive, and representative multilateralism was needed at a time of growing geopolitical tensions, conflicts, humanitarian crises, climate vulnerabilities and economic pressures. He further appreciated the UN chief’s “continued attention” to issues of particular importance to Pakistan, including regional peace and stability, counter-terrorism, climate vulnerability and development challenges. “We also greatly appreciate the UN’s consistent position on the Jammu and Kashmir dispute and the reiteration of the UN framework and UNSC resolutions for resolving the dispute,” he said. Dar said he briefed the UN chief on India’s unilateral move of holding the Indus Waters Treaty (IWT) in abeyance , which he referred to as a blatant violation of international law. “We underscored the need to ensure that India stops weaponising water and fulfils its obligations under the IWT.” He also highlighted Pakistan’s “deep concern” at the continued use of Afghan soil for carrying out terrorist attacks against Pakistan. He urged the UN chief and the international community to help address these challenges. Dar meets UN chief Earlier in the day, Dar held a one-on-one meeting with the UN chief, with the two discussing regional and global issues relating to peace and security, the Foreign Office (FO) said. The FO said the discussions covered Palestine, Jammu and Kashmir, Afghanistan, counter-terrorism and the future of multilateralism. Dar briefed the UN secretary general on Pakistan’s positions on Jammu and Kashmir and the Indus Waters Treaty (IWT), reaffirming Islamabad’s call for a just and peaceful resolution of the Kashmir dispute in accordance with relevant UNSC resolutions. According to the FO, Dar also highlighted Pakistan’s diplomatic efforts to promote dialogue and de-escalation, including its facilitation of the Islamabad talks between the US and Iran. He reaffirmed Pakistan’s commitment to dialogue and diplomacy as the most effective means of resolving disputes. The UN secretary general appreciated Pakistan’s longstanding contribution to the UN, as well as its diplomatic efforts to promote dialogue, mediation and de-escalation, the FO said. Guterres arrived in Islamabad in the early hours of Tuesday for a two-day official visit. “Upon arrival, the secretary-general was received by Acting Foreign Secretary Ambassador Nabeel Munir,” the FO said in a post on X. The visit comes as Guterres’ 10-year tenure as UN chief is set to end on Dec 31. During the visit, Guterres is set to meet President Asif Ali Zardari, Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif and Chief of Defence Forces and Chief of Army Staff Field Marshal Asim Munir, the FO said on Monday. The UN chief is also scheduled to visit the headquarters of the UNMOGIP and attend a briefing at the National Disaster Management Authority (NDMA) headquarters. In its Monday statement, the FO said that during Guterres’ visit, Pakistan’s “efforts towards strengthening multilateralism and international peace and security, as well as its strides towards disaster preparedness and early warning, will be highlighted”. PM Shehbaz met Guterres on the sidelines of the UN General Assembly in New York last month. The two discussed major regional and international developments, including the situation in the Middle East. In that meeting, Guterres commended Pakistan’s role and strong voice at the UN, as well as its contribution to international peace and security. The UN chief also appreciated Pakistan’s role and sacrifices in countering terrorism. Guterres’ first visit to Pakistan as the UN secretary general was in February 2020, about three years after he was elected to the position in 2016.

items.title: Techiman-Krobo Nursing Training principal to remain at post despite calls for her removal
items.description: The Ministry’s spokesperson, Tony Goodman, said the decision is based on the findings and recommendations of a committee set up to investigate the concerns that led to months of disruption at the school. Speaking on Adom FM’s Dwaso Nsem , Mr Goodman said although the committee acknowledged concerns about the principal’s approach to students, it did not find sufficient grounds to recommend her removal. He said the committee included the Krobohene, who, in his view, would not endorse wrongdoing or allow inappropriate conduct to go unchecked. “The Krobohene was part of the committee and will not supervise wrong things. He is principled,” he said. Mr Goodman acknowledged that the principal had not handled some matters appropriately and could at times be too strict with students. “We agree that there were things the woman was not doing right and was a bit hard on the students,” he said. However, he said the committee’s broader findings painted a troubling picture of the state of affairs at the institution, requiring measures to restore discipline and order. “But per the report, what was happening in the school wasn’t pleasing,” he said. Mr Goodman argued that the principal should therefore be given an opportunity to help restore sanity to the institution rather than being removed without a finding against her. “We should give the woman a chance to bring some sanity to the school,” he said. He described the situation at the school as having deteriorated into what he called a “free-for-all”, with serious concerns emerging about academic integrity. “It was a free-for-all,” he said. According to Mr Goodman, one of the issues uncovered during the committee’s work was an allegation that some students were paying for grades to enable them to progress to the next level of their education. He said such concerns demonstrated the need for stronger systems and discipline at the school. Mr Goodman maintained that if the committee had found the principal unfit to continue in office, the Health Minister would have acted on that recommendation. “If the report had said the principal wasn’t fit for purpose, I’m sure the minister would have implemented that,” he said. “But there was no fault-finding.” His comments come as authorities prepare to reopen the school following months of closure after students staged demonstrations over concerns about the administration and management of the institution. The Ministry says measures are being implemented to address the concerns raised, including strengthening the governance structure, introducing clearer guidelines on student conduct and training teaching and non-teaching staff before the phased reopening of the school. The controversy follows a protest by students of the Techiman-Krobo Nursing and Midwifery Training College over concerns about the administration of the institution. The protest subsequently attracted the attention of the community and authorities, leading to the establishment of an investigative committee by the Health Ministry.

Ghana cautions citizens over fraudulent jobs luring them to Zambia for cybercrime
items.description: The Ministry of Foreign Affairs has warned Ghanaians against fraudulent employment opportunities in Zambia following the arrest of six Ghanaian nationals in Lusaka in connection with an alleged organised cybercrime operation. In a travel advisory dated October 5, the Ministry said it had observed an emerging trend in which Ghanaians are lured to Zambia with seemingly legitimate job offers before being subjected to coercive conditions and forced to participate in cybercrime activities. The advisory follows a joint operation by the Zambia Police Service, the Drug Enforcement Commission (DEC) and the Department of Immigration on August 23. The operation targeted a facility suspected of being involved in organised cybercrime and resulted in the arrest of 79 people. Of those arrested, 10 were Zambians while 69 were foreign nationals, including six Ghanaians. According to the Ministry, information received by the Ghana High Commission in Lusaka indicates that some of the Ghanaians had travelled to Zambia after being recruited through what appeared to be legitimate employment opportunities. These included positions advertised as online data-entry jobs. However, the Ministry said some of the recruits were allegedly forced into online scam activities after their passports were confiscated by their employers. “The Ministry of Foreign Affairs has observed with concern the emerging trend of Ghanaians being lured to Zambia through fraudulent employment opportunities and subsequently being subjected to coercive conditions and forced involvement in cybercrime activities,” the advisory stated. It warned that the development points to an increasing tactic by human trafficking syndicates to exploit unsuspecting job seekers by using fraudulent employment offers as a means of recruiting them into illicit activities. “The above situation highlights the growing use of fraudulent employment opportunities by human trafficking syndicates to lure unsuspecting job seekers into illicit activities,” the Ministry said. The Ministry has consequently urged Ghanaians travelling to Zambia, particularly those seeking employment, to exercise extreme caution and conduct thorough checks before accepting job offers. It advised prospective job seekers to verify the authenticity of employment offers, recruitment agencies and prospective employers before making arrangements to travel. The Ministry also urged Ghanaians already living in Zambia to remain vigilant when responding to online employment opportunities. It further encouraged them to maintain regular contact with the Ghana High Commission in Lusaka and seek consular assistance when necessary. The advisory forms part of the government’s broader efforts to protect Ghanaians travelling to and residing outside the country. “The Ministry wishes to use this opportunity to reiterate government’s commitment to safeguarding the welfare and interests of Ghanaians travelling to or residing abroad,” it stated.
